- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

#### `metrics_events_create`

**Register an event**

Registers a new event name and (optionally) its typed properties. Only `name` is required.

If the name matches an existing **pending** (auto-discovered) row, this approves that row instead of returning a conflict. Otherwise an already-registered name returns `409`.

**Use cases**

- **Register a known event** — `{ "name": "checkout_completed" }` so metrics can reference it.
- **Declare typed properties** — supply `properties` to document the event's payload shape.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | `string` | Event name. Starts with a letter, digit, or `_`; letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `.`; max 50 characters. The cap is the Analytics Engine index budget — 96 bytes total, less a 36-byte project UUID and a separator — and the API has always enforced 50 while this spec advertised 128. The charset is ASCII, so characters and bytes are the same count. Immutable after create — this is the handle metric queries reference. _(pattern `^[a-zA-Z0-9_][a-zA-Z0-9_\-.]{0,49}$`)_ |
| `folder` | optional | `any` | Optional folder name grouping items in the dashboard. Alphanumeric, `_` or `-` (no `/`). Part of the SDK lookup key (`<folder>/<name>`). |
| `description` | optional | `string` | Optional human-readable description of the event. |
| `properties` | optional | `object[]` | Typed properties declared on the event. Defaults to an empty list. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `listToken` | optional | `string` | REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `metrics_events_list` call. It proves you listed existing metrics events and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `metrics_events_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `ALREADY_EXISTS` — A resource with this name already exists in the project.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.
- `PLAN_LIMIT` — The action would exceed a plan quota (e.g. the tier's maximum experiments, metrics, or configs). Upgrade the plan or archive an existing resource.

## Ops

Operational queue: the unified table of bug reports, feature requests, and
auto-filed error/alert tickets, all over `/api/admin/ops`. One `create`
endpoint files either user type (`type: bug | feature_request`); list, get,
update, and link-pr are unified across every type. Also exposes the
`notify` escalation bell and the read-only Slack-channels list used to
resolve alert-rule notification targets.

**Handles.** A queue item is addressed by its per-project `number` (e.g. `7`)
or its full id — the API resolves either.

### `ops_ack`

**Ack an item (start a run)**

Acknowledge a queue item — a person or an AI agent declaring "I'm on this
now". Opens a run: stamps who picked the item up and when, assigns them as
owner, and moves the item into the matching working status
(`investigating_by_ai` for an AI ack, `in_progress` for a human one). The
dashboard renders the open run as a live working indicator (which agent +
time since the run started).

**AI ack.** Pass `agent` with your own agent type (`claude`, `cursor`,
`copilot`, `jules`; `gemini` is also accepted and is normalized to `jules` on receipt) and, when you have one, the
run's `sessionId` so the dashboard can deep-link to the session. If the
project has no connected trigger connector of that type the call fails
with `AGENT_NOT_CONNECTED` — list the available agents with `ops agents list` and use one of those (or connect the agent under Settings →
Triggers).

**Launching.** When the named agent has a connected trigger and you pass
no `sessionId`, the ack also fires that trigger — a new provider run
starts working the item. Pass `launch: false` to only claim the item and
record the run (you are doing the work yourself), without starting one.
A launch on an item linked to others (see `group` on `ops get`) is only
allowed on the group's master — any other member answers `409`
`INVALID_TRANSITION`, naming the master to ack instead.

**Completion.** The run closes automatically on the loop's final actions —
linking the fixing PR (`link-pr`), an ops-notify escalation, or a
completion status change (`ready_for_qa`/`resolved`) — and the dashboard
then shows the run result (final action, PR, duration, session link).

**One session per item.** An AI ack on an item whose open run belongs to
another live agent session answers `409` `ALREADY_EXISTS`, naming that
run — skip the item, the other session is working it. Your own run is
adopted, not refused: re-ack with its `runId` (a fired run's prompt names
it; a previous ack returned it) or the same `sessionId`. A run a trigger
fire claimed is adopted by the FIRST session to ack it. A run silent past
the stuck-run threshold (6h), or `takeover: true`, is superseded instead.
A human ack never replaces an open agent run.

**Use case:** Call this first when picking an item up, so the team sees
who/what is working on it in real time.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules" \| "gemini" \| "jarvis"` | The AI agent type acking on the item's behalf — pass your own type when you are a coding agent (Claude Code passes `claude`, Cursor `cursor`, Copilot `copilot`, Jules `jules`, Gemini `gemini` → normalized to `jules`). Omit entirely for a human ack by the authenticated caller. |
| `sessionId` | optional | `string` | The agent-run session id (e.g. Claude's `session_01…`), so the dashboard can deep-link to the exact run page. Omit when the harness has no session id. _(length 0–300)_ |
| `launch` | optional | `boolean` | Whether an AI ack may FIRE the agent's connected trigger. Default `true`: an ack naming a connected agent, with no `sessionId`, starts a new provider run of that agent. Pass `false` to only record the ack — claim the item and open the run record — without starting anything, e.g. when you ARE that agent working the item yourself and have no session id to pass. Ignored on a human ack. _(default `true`)_ |
| `runId` | optional | `string` | The run you were handed — the investigation id a fired run's prompt names, or the `runId` an earlier ack returned. Proves the open run is yours, so the ack adopts it instead of answering `409` `ALREADY_EXISTS`. _(length 0–100)_ |
| `takeover` | optional | `boolean` | Replace another session's LIVE run on the item instead of being refused with `409` `ALREADY_EXISTS`. Only when you were asked to replace that session — two sessions on one item each open their own PR. _(default `false`)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `ALREADY_EXISTS` — A resource with this name already exists in the project.
- `AGENT_NOT_CONNECTED` — The named AI agent type has no connected trigger connector in this project — list the available agents (`ops agents list` / `GET /api/admin/agent-profiles`) and use one of those, or connect the agent under Settings → Triggers.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `ops_bug`

**File a bug report.**

Files one queue item — a bug report or a feature request — and fires the project's connectors (GitHub issue / Slack). `type` selects which; only the two user-fileable types are accepted (`error`/`alert` tickets are auto-filed by the platform). Returns the new id and per-project number.

**Use cases**

- **File a bug** — `{ "type": "bug", "title": "Checkout 500s on Safari", "stepsToReproduce": "…" }`.
- **File a feature request** — `{ "type": "feature_request", "title": "Dark mode", "priority": "nice_to_have" }`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | required | `string` | One-line bug title (no leading/trailing whitespace). _(length 1–200; pattern `^\S(.*\S)?$`)_ |
| `stepsToReproduce` | optional | `string` | How to reproduce the bug. _(default `""`; length 0–8000)_ |
| `actualResult` | optional | `string` | What actually happened. _(default `""`; length 0–8000)_ |
| `expectedResult` | optional | `string` | What was expected instead. _(default `""`; length 0–8000)_ |
| `priority` | optional | `any` | Initial triage priority, or `null`. |
| `status` | optional | `any` | Initial lifecycle status; defaults to `open` when omitted. |
| `assigneeId` | optional | `any` | The `users.id` of the person to assign as owner at creation, or `null`. |
| `delegateConnectorId` | optional | `string` | The agent connector the filer chose to delegate this item to at creation. When set, the server launches that one agent and skips any tag-rule auto-launch, so the filer's choice prevails and only one run starts. |
| `subscribers` | optional | `string[]` | Emails of teammates to subscribe to this item's Slack pings at creation. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `tags` | optional | `string[]` | Tag names to label the item with, e.g. `["ios", "checkout"]`. Each name is matched case-insensitively against the project's existing tags and reuses that tag (keeping its stored casing) when one matches; a name with no match creates a new project tag. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `reporterEmail` | optional | `any` | Email of the reporter, or `null`. |
| `pageUrl` | optional | `any` | URL of the page the bug relates to, or `null`. |
| `userAgent` | optional | `any` | Reporter's user-agent string, or `null`. |

### `ops_fired_alerts_list`

**List fired alerts**

Returns the project's FIRED alerts as a **bare JSON array** (no pagination envelope), ordered by `createdAt desc`. Defaults to the currently-firing ones (`status=active`); pass a `status` to widen to resolved/dismissed history or `all`.

A fired alert is an **instance** of an alert rule, and an instance IS its ops queue item — the same row `/api/admin/ops` returns with `type: "alert"`, viewed through the alert lens. One rule produces many instances over its life and at most one is open at a time: when the condition clears the instance closes, and the next firing is a NEW instance with its own id and history. That is why `severity` reads off the rule (the queue item carries it as `priority`) and why resolving the queue item and clearing the alert are one act, not two rows to keep in step.

Instances are opened only by the platform — the UI's killswitch handlers plus the worker's analysis consumer and alerts cron — never filed by hand, so this surface is list + triage (via PATCH), with no create. The rules that *define* metric-threshold alerts live at `/api/admin/alert-rules`.

**Use case:** Snapshot what is currently firing for an on-call view or the home Alerts block, or pull `status=all` to audit how a noisy rule has behaved over time.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `status` | optional | `"active" \| "resolved" \| "dismissed" \| "all"` | Filter by lifecycle state. Defaults to `active` (currently firing); `all` returns every status. _(default `"active"`)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).

### `ops_fired_alerts_noise`

**Mark a fired alert as noise**

Waves a fired alert off as **noise** — it closes as `dismissed` (the queue item goes `wont_fix`) and is recorded as noise rather than a plain dismissal — and optionally relaxes the rule that raised it so the same condition fires less often.

- **No `relax`** — mark as noise only; the rule is untouched.
- **`relax: "recommended"`** — apply the recommended suggestion from `GET /api/admin/alerts/{id}/relax-options`.
- **`relax: "<field>"`** (`threshold`, `rangeMin`, `rangeMax`, `sigma`, `requiredBuckets`, `windowHours`, `noDataMinutes`) without `value` — apply the computed suggestion for that field. `422` when the backtest has none for it, with the reason.
- **`relax: "<field>"` with `value`** — set that field to exactly `value`. It must be a relaxation (a higher `gt` threshold, a lower `lt` one, a wider range, a higher sigma, more required buckets, a longer window); a value that would make the rule fire more is refused with `422` — tighten a rule with `PATCH /api/admin/alert-rules/{id}`. Warning / recovery levels move by the same delta; a longer window pins the bucket width and keeps an "N of M" rule's ratio.

The rule change goes through the alert-rule update, so it is validated, audited, and restorable exactly like any other edit. The ops item records it as `context.alert.noise` — `{ by, at, relaxed: { field, dimension, from, to } | null }`. Returns the closed alert and the relaxation applied (or `null`).

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `relax` | optional | `any` | `recommended` applies the recommended suggestion; a field name applies that field's suggestion, or exactly `value` when given. Omit to leave the rule alone. |
| `value` | optional | `number` | Exact value for the `relax` field. Must loosen the rule. Requires `relax` to name a field. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `ops_fired_alerts_relax_options`

**Suggest how to relax a noisy alert's rule**

Computes, for one fired `metric_rule` alert, the smallest change to its rule that would have kept THIS firing quiet — one suggestion per dimension the rule can be relaxed on:

- **value** — the bound itself: `threshold`, a range edge (`rangeMin` / `rangeMax`), or `sigma` for anomaly / outlier rules. A warning or recovery level moves by the same delta, so their ordering survives.
- **buckets** — `requiredBuckets`, on a rule that already counts "N of M" breaching buckets.
- **time** — `windowHours` (or `noDataMinutes` for a no-data rule). The bucket width is pinned at its current size, so the window grows by buckets rather than widening them.

No model is involved. The suggestions come from a **backtest**: the rule is replayed over the metric's recent data (up to 7 days plus the firing) with the evaluator's own arithmetic and raise/clear state machine, and each knob is searched for the smallest value whose replay never has this alert open, plus a little headroom, rounded to a number a person would type. Each option reports how often the rule fired over the replayed span before and after the change. The `recommended` option is the one that gives up the fewest OTHER firings (ties go to the smaller change).

Read-only — nothing changes. Apply a suggestion with `POST /api/admin/alerts/{id}/noise`. An alert not raised by a metric rule (kill switch, experiment guards), or whose rule is archived or composite, is a `422` — it has no rule knob to relax, though it can still be marked as noise.

**Use case:** before marking an alert as noise, see what it would take for the rule to stop raising it, and what that costs in coverage.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

### `ops_fired_alerts_update`

**Update a fired alert**

Triage writes on one fired alert — the only mutations this surface allows. All body fields are optional (at least one required); only the fields present are changed.

- **`status`** — flip between `active` / `resolved` / `dismissed`. `resolved` and `dismissed` stamp `resolvedAt` / `dismissedAt`; `active` re-opens and clears both. These write the underlying queue item's own status (`resolved` / `wont_fix` / `open`), so clearing an alert here and resolving it in the ops queue are the same act. A cleared instance is never revived: if the condition fires again it opens a NEW instance with its own id.
- **`assigneeId`** — the PERSON owner (a `users.id`), or `null` to unassign.
- **`agent`** — the AGENT owner: a connected trigger connector's id, or the built-in `"jarvis"` (**Enterprise plan only** — `403` otherwise), or `null` to clear. Person and agent halves are independent.

Returns the updated row; `404` if the alert does not exist in the project.

**Use cases**

- **Wave off a known condition** — `{ "status": "dismissed" }` on an alert that needs no action.
- **Hand it to someone** — `{ "assigneeId": "…" }` from the ops cockpit's Owner column.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `status` | optional | `"active" \| "resolved" \| "dismissed"` | New lifecycle state, written through to the queue item (`resolved` / `wont_fix` / `open`). `resolved` / `dismissed` stamp their timestamp; `active` re-opens and clears both. |
| `assigneeId` | optional | `any` | PERSON owner — a `users.id`, or `null` to clear the assignment. |
| `agent` | optional | `any` | AGENT owner — a connected trigger connector's id (`connectors.id`), the built-in `"jarvis"` (Enterprise plan only — rejected with `403` otherwise), or `null` to clear. Stored in `assigneeConnectorId` or `assigneeAgent` depending on the value; the two are mutually exclusive. |

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `ops_get`

**Get one queue item**

Fetch a single queue item by its per-project `number` or full id.

An item linked to others (blocked by / blocking / duplicate of) carries its `group`: every connected item, and the `master` agent runs work through. Pass `include=linked` to inline the other members' content as `linkedItems`, so one call reads the whole group.

A public bug or feature request filed with the reporter's SDK identity carries `context.reporter`: who filed it (their user attributes) and the feature flags, kill switches and experiment groups they had on when they filed it. Read it before you investigate. A bug that only some users hit is often caused by one of those. Reproduce with the same state (a flag whitelist or an experiment override) before you rule them out. It is a snapshot from filing time, so check the entity's current state too.

**Use cases**

- **Inspect one item** before updating its status or linking a PR.
- **Pick up linked work** — `include=linked` reads the master and everything tied to it before a run starts.
- **Debug a public report** against the reporter's own feature state in `context.reporter`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `include` | optional | `"linked"` | `linked` inlines the content of every other member of the item's link group as `linkedItems`. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

### `ops_group`

**Update a linked group**

Applies `status` and/or `priority` to every item in this item's link group — the items tied to it, directly or through a chain, by blocked-by / blocking / duplicate-of links (see `group` on `ops get`). Each member goes through the normal item update, so activity, audit, run close-out and the error sync happen exactly as for a one-item edit. Members already in the requested state are left alone. An item with no links is a group of one.

**Use cases**

- **The fix landed for the whole group** — `{ "status": "resolved" }` on any member.
- **Drop the group** — `{ "status": "wont_fix" }`.
- **Escalate it together** — `{ "priority": "critical" }`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `status` | optional | `"open" \| "pending_approval" \| "investigating_by_ai" \| "in_progress" \| "blocked" \| "ready_for_qa" \| "resolved" \| "wont_fix"` | Lifecycle status of a queue item. The working flow is `open` → `in_progress` → `ready_for_qa` → `resolved` (or `wont_fix`, terminal from any earlier stage). `blocked` marks an item that can't progress until an external dependency clears — a working state a human sets and clears. `ready_for_qa` is what a developer sets once a fix lands; `resolved` is the QA sign-off, normally flipped in the dashboard after verification — set it directly from code only when the fix has been verified end-to-end. `investigating_by_ai` is a system-owned display state — set when the AI agent (Jarvis) picks an item up to investigate, never chosen by a human — so it is shown but not offered as a manual choice. `pending_approval` is the one human-gated holding state: it parks an item OUT of the work queue until a human promotes it to `open` in the dashboard, so `GET /api/admin/ops` excludes it under `status=all`/default and returns it only when requested as an exact `status`. It covers untriaged inbound that must never be auto-implemented — connector requests filed from a customer's connectors panel, and questions funnelled in from the "Stuck in onboarding?" assistant — where approving means flipping the status to `open`. Two earlier values were removed in favour of this single gate: `triage` (the onboarding-help bucket, now `pending_approval`) and `triaged` (a redundant "looked at but not started" step, now plain `open`). |
| `priority` | optional | `any` | Triage priority, or `null` when not set (in an update, `null` clears it). |

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `ops_links`

**Link related items**

Edits how this queue item relates to others: which items block it ("blocked by"), which items it blocks ("blocking"), and which item it duplicates ("duplicate of"). The blocker lists are incremental — already-linked or never-linked items are no-ops and every other relation is left as is; `duplicateOf` sets or (with `null`) clears the one canonical item. An item with a blocker that is not `resolved`/`wont_fix` sits in the dashboard's Blocked lane. The relations show on `ops get` as `blockedBy` / `blocking` / `duplicateOf` / `duplicates`.

A link that would make an item block or duplicate itself — directly or through a chain — is rejected with `409`; an item from another project doesn't resolve (`404`). Marking an item a duplicate of a still-open item closes it as `wont_fix`; if the canonical is already `resolved`/`wont_fix` (or the item itself is already closed) its status is left alone.

**Use cases**

- **This item can't move until #12 lands** — `{ "addBlockedBy": ["12"] }`.
- **Split work: this item gates #20 and #21** — `{ "addBlocking": ["20", "21"] }`.
- **The dependency turned out not to be one** — `{ "removeBlockedBy": ["12"] }`.
- **Same bug was filed twice** — `{ "duplicateOf": "8" }` on the newer item — it closes as `wont_fix` while #8 is open.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `addBlockedBy` | optional | `string[]` | Items (number or id) to record as blocking this one. Already-linked items are a no-op. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `removeBlockedBy` | optional | `string[]` | Items (number or id) to stop recording as blocking this one. Unlinked items are a no-op. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `addBlocking` | optional | `string[]` | Items (number or id) this one blocks. Already-linked items are a no-op. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `removeBlocking` | optional | `string[]` | Items (number or id) this one should stop blocking. Unlinked items are a no-op. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `duplicateOf` | optional | `any` | Mark this item as a duplicate of another (number or id), replacing any earlier canonical; `null` clears it. Omit to leave it unchanged. While the canonical is still open, the item closes as `wont_fix`; a canonical that is already `resolved`/`wont_fix` leaves the item's status alone. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `ops_list`

**List the operational queue**

Returns the unified ops queue (bugs, feature requests, errors, alerts, measurement plans) in work order — highest priority first, oldest first within a priority — so consumers work it top-down. Every filter is applied in SQL before paging, and filters combine with AND. Human-gated holding states (items awaiting human sign-off in the dashboard) are never returned by `all`/default status.

**Filters:** `type` (one item type), `status` (one lifecycle status, or `unresolved` — everything not yet `resolved`/`wont_fix`), `priority` (one triage priority), `owner` (one person or agent), `reporter` (one filer's email), `closedSince` (drop items closed before a time), and `scope=ready` — the items ready to be picked up right now: `open`, with nobody working them (no open run), and either unowned or reopened (sent back to `open` after an earlier run finished).

**Paging:** `limit` is the page size and `offset` the number of items to skip. The order is stable, so walk the queue with `offset += limit`; a page shorter than `limit` is the last one.

**Use case:** Pull the open queue to triage — e.g. every `bug` still `open` — before working items down one by one.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `type` | optional | `any` | Filter by item type, or `all` (the default). Every type a returned item can carry is filterable, including the auto-filed ones. _(default `"all"`)_ |
| `status` | optional | `any` | Filter by one lifecycle status, `unresolved` for every status that is not `resolved` or `wont_fix`, or `all` for every status. Defaults to `all` over HTTP; the CLI and MCP tool default to `unresolved`, so pass `all` there to include resolved and won't-fix items. The human-gated holding state (`pending_approval`) is excluded from `unresolved` and `all`, and returned only when requested as the exact status. _(default `"unresolved"`)_ |
| `priority` | optional | `any` | Filter by triage priority, or `all` (the default). Items with no priority set are returned only under `all`. _(default `"all"`)_ |
| `scope` | optional | `"all" \| "ready"` | `ready` narrows to the items ready to be picked up right now: status `open`, no open run (nobody has acked it and is still working), and either unowned (no person and no agent) or reopened (sent back to `open` after an earlier run finished). Leave `status` unset with it. `all` (the default) applies no such narrowing. _(default `"all"`)_ |
| `qaQuestions` | optional | `"all" \| "open"` | `open` narrows to the items with at least one unanswered QA question — the backlog QA answers first (read each with `ops get`, answer with `ops qa-questions answer`). `all` (the default) applies no such narrowing. _(default `"all"`)_ |
| `limit` | required | `integer` | Page size — max items to return (1–500). A page shorter than `limit` is the last one. _(1–500)_ |
| `offset` | optional | `integer` | Number of items to skip before the page starts. Defaults to 0. The order is stable, so `offset += limit` walks the queue page by page. _(default `0`; 0–100000)_ |
| `owner` | optional | `string` | Narrow to items owned by one person OR one agent. Matches a person by `users.id`, email, or display name, and an agent by connector id, display name, or kebab-case handle — e.g. `owner=Claude` or `owner=alice@acme.dev`. Case-insensitive exact match. |
| `reporter` | optional | `string` | Narrow to items filed by one reporter — an email, matched case-insensitive and exact against `reporterEmail`. Items with no reporter never match. While set, `status=all` also returns `pending_approval` items: public intake files every ticket as `pending_approval`, and a reporter must see the ticket they just filed. |
| `closedSince` | optional | `string` | ISO-8601 timestamp. Items still being worked are always returned; `resolved` and `wont_fix` items only when they closed at or after this time (see `closedAt`). Combines with `status` like any other filter. _(format: date-time)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).

### `ops_notify`

**Raise an attention notification**

Raise a 'needs your attention' bell notification. Create-only and idempotent on `dedupeKey` — re-raising with the same key updates the one card instead of stacking duplicates. It never reads, marks read, or deletes the feed, so it is safe for restricted ops keys.

**Use case:** Escalate work that can't land in code (a product decision, a credential only a human has, a resource only a human may edit), deduped so repeats don't spam the bell.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | required | `string` | One-line headline of what's blocked. _(length 1–200)_ |
| `summary` | required | `string` | One sentence: why it can't be fixed in code. Renders markdown. _(length 1–280)_ |
| `steps` | optional | `string[]` | Ordered steps the human should take to unblock — self-contained (the human reads only this card, not the agent's transcript), 3–6 steps, each naming the exact file, command, env var, or dashboard page. Renders markdown. |
| `href` | optional | `any` | Dashboard-relative deep link to the related item. `null` is accepted and treated as "no link". |
| `dedupeKey` | optional | `string` | Stable per-escalation key (e.g. `feedback:7`) so re-runs dedupe to one row. |

### `ops_qa_notes_create`

**Add a QA note to an item**

Append one typed QA note to a queue item. `kind` is `narrowing` (what now
passes vs what still fails), `clarification` (what "fixed" now means),
`verification` (requires a `verdict` of `pass` or `fail`, and `body` says
what was checked) or `correction` (withdraws an earlier framing). Notes
are append-only and appear in the item's QA notes section, not in the
comment thread. The author is the caller's identity; pass `agent` to
record the note as written by that agent type's QA automation. A `fail` verdict never changes the item's
status by itself: the dashboard offers an explicit "Reopen item" action,
and `ops update --status open` does the same from the CLI.

**Use case:** QA automation records "verified on production: FAIL, the
second facet still errors" as data an agent can read back.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `kind` | required | `"narrowing" \| "clarification" \| "verification" \| "correction"` | What a QA note is — `narrowing` (only part of the bug still fails), `clarification` (changes what "fixed" means), `verification` (a pass/fail verdict on a fix) or `correction` (withdraws an earlier framing). |
| `body` | required | `string` | The note (markdown). _(length 1–10000)_ |
| `verdict` | optional | `"pass" \| "fail"` | The outcome a `verification` note records. |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | The agent type writing the note — pass your own type when you are QA automation. Omitted, the note is attributed to the caller's identity. |
| `listToken` | optional | `string` | REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `ops_qa_notes_list` call. It proves you listed existing ops qa notes and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `ops_qa_notes_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

### `ops_routing_rules_create`

**Create a tag automation rule**

Appends one rule after the existing ones; existing rules are untouched.
The rule fires on a newly filed item carrying any of `tags` (or whose type
is in `types`) and applies its actions: `user` assigns a person,
`connector` hands the item to a connected coding agent (launching a run,
steered by `agentPrompt`), `status` / `priority` set triage fields, and
`subscribers` emails people. Tags are created on first use.

Returns `400` when the rule has no tag or type, or no action. Returns the
full rule list after the append.

**Use cases**

- **Auto-fix** — tag `ai-fix` hands the item to a connected agent with a steering prompt.
- **Triage** — every `error` ticket goes to `high` priority and an on-call email.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `tags` | optional | `string[]` | Tag names the rule matches (case-insensitive). Tags are created on first use. |
| `types` | optional | `"error" \| "alert" \| "bug" \| "feature_request"[]` | Ticket types the rule also fires on. |
| `enabled` | optional | `boolean` | Whether the rule is live. Defaults to `true`. |
| `user` | optional | `string` | Person to assign — a user id. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `connector` | optional | `string` | Connected coding agent to hand the item to — a connector id from `ops agents list`. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `agentPrompt` | optional | `string` | Steering prompt for the launched agent. Only kept alongside a `connector`. _(length 0–4000)_ |
| `status` | optional | `"open" \| "pending_approval" \| "investigating_by_ai" \| "in_progress" \| "blocked" \| "ready_for_qa" \| "resolved" \| "wont_fix"` | Lifecycle status of a queue item. The working flow is `open` → `in_progress` → `ready_for_qa` → `resolved` (or `wont_fix`, terminal from any earlier stage). `blocked` marks an item that can't progress until an external dependency clears — a working state a human sets and clears. `ready_for_qa` is what a developer sets once a fix lands; `resolved` is the QA sign-off, normally flipped in the dashboard after verification — set it directly from code only when the fix has been verified end-to-end. `investigating_by_ai` is a system-owned display state — set when the AI agent (Jarvis) picks an item up to investigate, never chosen by a human — so it is shown but not offered as a manual choice. `pending_approval` is the one human-gated holding state: it parks an item OUT of the work queue until a human promotes it to `open` in the dashboard, so `GET /api/admin/ops` excludes it under `status=all`/default and returns it only when requested as an exact `status`. It covers untriaged inbound that must never be auto-implemented — connector requests filed from a customer's connectors panel, and questions funnelled in from the "Stuck in onboarding?" assistant — where approving means flipping the status to `open`. Two earlier values were removed in favour of this single gate: `triage` (the onboarding-help bucket, now `pending_approval`) and `triaged` (a redundant "looked at but not started" step, now plain `open`). |
| `priority` | optional | `"nice_to_have" \| "medium" \| "high" \| "critical"` | Triage priority of a queue item. The lowest tier is `nice_to_have` (not `low`) — carried over from the feature-request "importance" scale this priority set replaced. |
| `subscribers` | optional | `string[]` | Emails notified about matching items. |
| `skipApproval` | optional | `boolean` | Let a matching public-intake ticket skip `pending_approval`. Defaults to `false`. |
| `listToken` | optional | `string` | REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `ops_routing_rules_list` call. It proves you listed existing ops routing rules and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `ops_routing_rules_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).

| `measured.blocking` | required | `boolean` | Whether a failing gate blocks the merge (a non-blocking gate only reports). |

| `guarded.enabled` | required | `boolean` | Whether the gate is evaluated at all. |
| `guarded.blocking` | required | `boolean` | Whether a failing gate blocks the merge (a non-blocking gate only reports). |
| `copy` | optional | `object` | Release gate. Passes when every copy i18n key exists in every published locale of its profile. Off by default. _(default `{"enabled":false,"blocking":false}`)_ |
| `copy.enabled` | required | `boolean` | Whether the gate is evaluated at all. |
| `copy.blocking` | required | `boolean` | Whether a failing gate blocks the merge (a non-blocking gate only reports). |
| `plan` | optional | `object` | Gate. Passes when every release resource the trail's approved plan lists exists on the trail (a flag, kill switch or experiment the person chose while the plan was made). Reads `pending` while a drafted plan waits for approval, and is left out when the trail has no plan yet. On and blocking by default, whoever approved the plan. _(default `{"enabled":true,"blocking":true}`)_ |
| `plan.enabled` | required | `boolean` | Whether the gate is evaluated at all. |
| `plan.blocking` | required | `boolean` | Whether a failing gate blocks the merge. Off, the gate only reports. |
| `requirePlan` | optional | `boolean` | Whether a person approves a trail's plan before it builds. Every trail is planned first — starting an agent on a trail with no approved plan fires a read-only plan run, and the build follows the approved plan. On, the plan run asks the person only what the goal leaves open (never how it ships — it chooses that itself), and the plan waits for their approval. Off, it asks nothing and takes its own recommendations; a plan the checks raise no warning on approves itself and the build starts, one with a warning waits for a person. _(default `true`)_ |
| `fixRounds` | optional | `integer` | How many times the server re-fires the coding agent with a fix prompt after a change's evals or findings fail. After the cap the trail reads `reviewing`, needs a person. `0` turns the loop off. _(default `3`; 0–10)_ |
| `goalWindowDays` | optional | `integer` | How many days a delivered trail is watched before its goal metric is judged. A trail is delivered when its plan is approved, every code and tracking item is done and every flag it ships behind is fully rolled out (or, with none, something merged). _(default `7`; 1–90)_ |
| `maxGoalReplans` | optional | `integer` | How many times shipeasy re-plans a trail on its own after its goal was missed. Each re-plan proposes new options that differ from what was tried. Past the cap the trail is off track and the owner decides; `0` never re-plans automatically. _(default `3`; 0–10)_ |
| `maxParallelRuns` | optional | `integer` | How many item runs a trail's build keeps working at once. A build launches an item run for each open item of the current milestone, up to this many; the rest wait for a slot. _(default `3`; 1–10)_ |
| `attributionWindowHours` | optional | `integer` | How long after a trail merged an error or alert ticket may be attributed to it. Trails merged inside the window are offered to the investigating agent as candidates. _(default `72`; 1–720)_ |
| `rollout` | optional | `object` | How the flag a trail ships behind is ramped after merge — the release controller's plan (see the design doc, the release controller). Part of the plan's release block; the project's defaults live in `trail-gates` `rollout`. The controller runs on the alerts cron, so a hold shorter than the cron interval rounds up to the next tick. |
| `rollout.steps` | required | `number[]` | Percent steps, each above the one before, the last 100. |
| `rollout.holdMinutes` | required | `integer` | Minutes a step must stay healthy before the next one. _(0–10080)_ |
| `rollout.minExposure` | required | `integer` | Evaluations a step must have served before it counts as healthy, so a quiet hour never passes as a green one. `0` = no floor. _(≥ 0)_ |
| `rollout.internal` | optional | `any` | The team stage before any public percent — the project's members are allowlisted on the flag (by email) and the step holds like any other. `null` or absent = no team stage. |
| `rollout.guards` | required | `object` | What is watched while a step holds. The trail's `guards` alert-rule resources are watched too. |
| `rollout.guards.alertRuleIds` | required | `string[]` | Alert rules (ids) whose firing during a step is a breach. |
| `rollout.guards.experimentGuardrails` | required | `boolean` | Whether a breached guardrail of the trail's measuring experiment is a breach. |
| `rollout.guards.attributedErrors` | required | `boolean` | Whether a new error attributed to the trail at high confidence is a breach. |
| `rollout.policies` | required | `object` | The three rollout decisions — the project defaults unless the creation dialog or a plan edit sets them. |
| `rollout.policies.onBreach` | required | `"pull_back" \| "ask_first" \| "ask_then_pull_back"` | What to do when a guard trips during a step — `pull_back` (pull the flag back, investigate and suggest a fix, tell the owner; the default), `ask_first` (ask the owner, only notify), or `ask_then_pull_back` (ask, and pull back after `breachTimeoutMinutes` with no answer). |
| `rollout.policies.breachTimeoutMinutes` | required | `integer` | With `ask_then_pull_back`, minutes the owner has before the controller pulls back. _(1–1440)_ |
| `rollout.policies.advance` | required | `"auto" \| "ask"` | Whether a healthy step advances by itself (`auto`) or waits for the owner to say so (`ask`). |
| `rollout.policies.afterFix` | required | `"resume" \| "ask" \| "restart"` | What happens when the fix merges — `resume` from the last healthy step, `ask` the owner first, or `restart` from the first step. |
| `autopilot` | optional | `object` | What autopilot may do and spend on one trail. Crossing any one pauses it at a safe point and hands the trail to its owner. The project's defaults live in `trail-gates` `autopilot`. |
| `autopilot.maxRisk` | required | `any` | The highest Risk agent score (0-100) autopilot may merge at. `null` = no risk limit. With a limit set, a change the Risk agent has not scored (or no Risk agent at all) is a limit hit, never a pass. |
| `autopilot.repos` | required | `string[]` | Repos (`owner/repo`) autopilot may act in. Empty = any repo the trail may touch. |
| `autopilot.types` | required | `"feature" \| "bug" \| "task"[]` | Trail types autopilot may act on. Empty = any. |
| `autopilot.maxFixRounds` | required | `integer` | Fix rounds per change before autopilot hands the trail over. _(0–10)_ |
| `autopilot.maxPullBacks` | required | `integer` | Pull-backs of the rollout before autopilot hands the trail over. _(0–10)_ |
| `autopilot.maxRuns` | required | `integer` | Agent runs autopilot may start in all (build, fix and investigation runs). _(0–100)_ |
| `intakeMatching` | optional | `boolean` | Whether new and still-open errors, alerts, bugs and feature requests are compared with the project's open trails. A confident match attaches the item to the trail with the evidence; a weak one lands under the trail's possibly related list for its owner to confirm or reject. Matching never creates a trail. _(default `true`)_ |
| `repos` | optional | `object` | Per-repo overrides keyed by `owner/repo`. An override replaces the project's `checks.required` for changes in that repo; every other gate stays project-wide. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `ops_update`

**Update a queue item**

Update a queue item. The body is validated against the item's stored type: a `bug` accepts its content fields (title, steps-to-reproduce, actual/expected result) plus `status`/`priority`/`notify` and a GitHub PR link; a `feature_request` its content (title, description, use-case) plus the same triage fields; `error`/`alert`/`measure_plan` accept `status`/`priority`/`notify` only (their content is platform-owned). Pass at least one field.

Completing an `error` ticket (status `resolved` or `ready_for_qa`) also resolves the tracked error it links to; the error reopens automatically if it recurs — so completing is safe pre-deploy.

**Use cases**

- **Start working an item** — `{ "status": "in_progress" }`.
- **Hand off for review** — `{ "status": "ready_for_qa" }` once the fix landed (the mode PR-based loops use).
- **Triage** — `{ "priority": "high" }`, content edits on bug/feature items.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `title` | optional | `string` | New bug title (no leading/trailing whitespace). _(length 1–200; pattern `^\S(.*\S)?$`)_ |
| `stepsToReproduce` | optional | `string` | Updated reproduction steps. _(length 0–8000)_ |
| `actualResult` | optional | `string` | Updated actual result. _(length 0–8000)_ |
| `expectedResult` | optional | `string` | Updated expected result. _(length 0–8000)_ |
| `status` | optional | `"open" \| "pending_approval" \| "investigating_by_ai" \| "in_progress" \| "blocked" \| "ready_for_qa" \| "resolved" \| "wont_fix"` | Lifecycle status of a queue item. The working flow is `open` → `in_progress` → `ready_for_qa` → `resolved` (or `wont_fix`, terminal from any earlier stage). `blocked` marks an item that can't progress until an external dependency clears — a working state a human sets and clears. `ready_for_qa` is what a developer sets once a fix lands; `resolved` is the QA sign-off, normally flipped in the dashboard after verification — set it directly from code only when the fix has been verified end-to-end. `investigating_by_ai` is a system-owned display state — set when the AI agent (Jarvis) picks an item up to investigate, never chosen by a human — so it is shown but not offered as a manual choice. `pending_approval` is the one human-gated holding state: it parks an item OUT of the work queue until a human promotes it to `open` in the dashboard, so `GET /api/admin/ops` excludes it under `status=all`/default and returns it only when requested as an exact `status`. It covers untriaged inbound that must never be auto-implemented — connector requests filed from a customer's connectors panel, and questions funnelled in from the "Stuck in onboarding?" assistant — where approving means flipping the status to `open`. Two earlier values were removed in favour of this single gate: `triage` (the onboarding-help bucket, now `pending_approval`) and `triaged` (a redundant "looked at but not started" step, now plain `open`). |
| `priority` | optional | `any` | Triage priority, or `null` when not set (in an update, `null` clears it). |
| `githubPrNumber` | optional | `any` | Link (or, when `null`, unlink) a GitHub pull request to this bug. |
| `notify` | optional | `any` | Where this item's completion notification lands, or `null`. |
| `description` | optional | `string` | Updated description. _(length 0–8000)_ |
| `useCase` | optional | `string` | Updated use case. _(length 0–8000)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### Alerts

Alert rules: the metric-threshold definitions the analysis cron evaluates each run.

**What fires.** Each rule binds a `metricId`, a `comparator` (`gt`/`gte`/`lt`/`lte`), and a `threshold`. On every cron pass the cron aggregates the metric over the trailing `windowHours` and raises an alert at `severity` when `value comparator threshold` holds.

**Immutable metric.** The bound metric (and its aggregation) is fixed at create time — there is no update path for `metricId`. Tune `threshold`/`comparator`/`windowHours`/`severity`/`name`/`enabled` instead, or delete + recreate to repoint the rule at a different metric.

**Delivery.** `notify` optionally targets a Slack channel and/or email for this rule; `null` falls back to the project's default notification settings. Slack targets require a connected Slack connector.

#### `ops_alerts_archive`

**Delete an alert rule**

Deletes the alert rule. The cron stops evaluating it immediately. Use this (then create a new rule) to repoint alerting at a different metric, since `metricId` is immutable.

**Use case:** Remove an alert rule that is no longer needed, or as the first half of repointing a rule at a different metric.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

#### `ops_alerts_create`

**Create an alert rule**

Creates a metric-threshold alert rule. `name`, `metricId`, `comparator`, and `threshold` are required; `windowHours` defaults to `24`, `severity` to `warn`, and `enabled` to `true`.

Returns `404` if `metricId` does not resolve, and `400` for a metric with no scalar form over a window (e.g. retention metrics) — the cron can't evaluate those.

**Use cases**

- **Threshold alert** — warn when an error/latency metric crosses a value over a rolling window.
- **Routed alert** — set `notify` to page a specific Slack channel or on-call email instead of the project default.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | required | `string` | Human label for the rule, shown on the alert and the rules list. _(length 1–120)_ |
| `metricId` | required | `string` | Id of the metric to evaluate. _(length 1–∞)_ |
| `kind` | optional | `"normal" \| "anomaly" \| "outliers" \| "no_data" \| "composite"` | What the rule watches for. `normal` compares the metric's own value — against `threshold` via `comparator`, or against the [`rangeMin`, `rangeMax`] corridor it must stay inside. `anomaly` compares it against its own seasonal baseline in sigmas: the same fit a chart draws as the band, so a point outside the drawn band is exactly a breaching bucket, and one metric can back rules at several sigmas. `outliers` compares each `by()` group against its peers in the same bucket and is refused on a metric with no grouping. _(default `"normal"`)_ |
| `comparator` | optional | `"gt" \| "gte" \| "lt" \| "lte"` | How the metric value is compared to the threshold. Read only by a `normal` rule with no range set. _(default `"gt"`)_ |
| `threshold` | optional | `number` | Threshold the metric value is compared against. Required for a `normal` rule unless a range is given; ignored by every other kind. |
| `rangeMin` | optional | `any` | Lower edge of the corridor the metric must stay inside. Setting either bound switches a `normal` rule off `comparator`/`threshold` and onto the range, which breaches on LEAVING it in either direction. One bound alone is a one-sided range. |
| `rangeMax` | optional | `any` | Upper edge of the corridor the metric must stay inside. |
| `sigma` | optional | `any` | How far from normal is too far, for `anomaly` and `outliers`, in sigma-equivalents. Omit (or `null`) for 3, which is also the half-width of the band a chart draws — so an unconfigured rule fires exactly where the picture says it would. |
| `direction` | optional | `any` | Which side of the baseline an `anomaly` or `outliers` rule watches. Omit (or `null`) for either, which is what "is this unusual" means; name a side for a metric that is only bad in one direction. |
| `sustained` | optional | `boolean` | Judge the window by ACCUMULATED departure instead of bucket by bucket. The ordinary check asks every bucket to be past `sigma`, which a slow regression never manages: a metric running 1.5σ worse than normal since Tuesday puts no single bucket past 3σ and pages nobody. A sustained rule adds up each bucket's excess over half a sigma and fires once the total passes twice `sigma` — four buckets at 2σ do it, a lone 3σ spike does not. `anomaly` and `outliers` only, and refused alongside `requiredBuckets`: the accumulated bar IS the evidence bar, and a second one counted in buckets would silently override it. _(default `false`)_ |
| `windowHours` | optional | `integer` | Lookback window (hours) the metric is aggregated over. 1–720. _(default `24`; 1–720)_ |
| `bucketMinutes` | optional | `any` | Width of the buckets the window is split into, in minutes. Omit (or `null`) to divide the window into 12 equal buckets. The rule is judged per bucket, so this is the resolution at which "sustained" is measured — a short bucket asks the condition to hold through finer detail. |
| `requiredBuckets` | optional | `any` | How many buckets must breach before the rule fires. Omit (or `null`) to require every bucket that had data. Buckets with nothing in them are excluded before this is counted, so on a sparse metric `null` can mean a single bucket — set this to 2 or more where one lone sample must never page. |
| `warnThreshold` | optional | `any` | The milder bound — a second level, in the same unit the kind judges in, that raises a quieter alert before the firing level is reached. Must be strictly milder than the level the rule fires at, or it could never fire on its own. Refused on a range rule and on a `sustained` one: neither condition is a single number, so there is nothing to substitute. |
| `recoveryThreshold` | optional | `any` | What the metric must get back to before a live alert closes. Without it a metric sitting on its threshold pages and clears once per tick. Must be on the safe side of the firing level, or equal to it. Omit (or `null`) for no hysteresis. |
| `groupAlerts` | optional | `boolean` | Fire one alert per `by()` group instead of one for the whole metric. The firing key becomes (rule, group), so each group raises, dedupes and recovers on its own. Refused on a metric with no `by()`, and on `no_data` — a group that went silent has no rows left to be missing from. _(default `false`)_ |
| `maxGroups` | optional | `any` | How many groups this rule may alert on at once. Omit (or `null`) for 10. Past the cap the worst groups fire and the count of the rest is stated on each ticket — a group set is customer data, and an uncapped rule on `by(user_id)` would file a ticket per user. |
| `noDataMinutes` | optional | `any` | For a `no_data` rule: how long the silence must last. Omit (or `null`) for 15 minutes. Five is the floor — below it, ordinary ingest lag empties the trailing bucket and reads as an outage. |
| `delayMinutes` | optional | `any` | Hold the evaluated window back this far behind live, on top of the reader's own settle grace. For a metric assembled from a source that lands in batches, whose trailing buckets are legitimately incomplete for longer than the grace covers. |
| `autoResolveMinutes` | optional | `any` | Close a live instance that has gone this long without a fresh verdict. A rule that cannot reach a verdict deliberately leaves its alert alone, which is right for a tick and wrong for a week. Never closes an instance that is currently breaching. Omit (or `null`) to never auto-resolve. |
| `composite` | optional | `object` | What a `composite` rule is a boolean over. `rules` are sibling alert-rule ids in the same project and `op` is how their states combine. A child's state is what the current pass concluded about it, falling back to whether it has an open instance — so a composite still means something on a tick where a child could not be evaluated, which is exactly the tick a "two of these are broken at once" rule is for. One level deep: a child may not itself be composite. |
| `composite.op` | required | `"and" \| "or"` | How the children's states combine. |
| `composite.rules` | required | `string[]` | Ids of the alert rules to combine. Stored sorted and de-duplicated. |
| `severity` | optional | `"danger" \| "warn" \| "info"` | Severity of the raised alert. A `warnThreshold` breach opens one step quieter than this. _(default `"warn"`)_ |
| `enabled` | optional | `boolean` | Whether the rule is evaluated by the cron. _(default `true`)_ |
| `notify` | optional | `any` | Delivery target for a rule's alert; `null` = use the project default. The `NotificationTarget` shape plus the in-app switch. |
| `listToken` | optional | `string` | REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `ops_alerts_list` call. It proves you listed existing ops alerts and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `ops_alerts_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

- `METRIC_NOT_FOUND` — The referenced metric does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `REFERENCED_NOT_FOUND` — A referenced entity (universe, metric, gate, event) does not exist.

#### `ops_alerts_list`

**List alert rules**

Returns every alert rule in the project (not paginated). Each rule carries its bound `metricId`, the denormalised `metricName` (or `null` if the metric was removed), the comparator/threshold/window, severity, enabled flag, and delivery target.

**Use case:** Audit which metrics have alerting configured — for example to confirm an on-call threshold is set before a launch.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | optional | `string` | Case-insensitive substring filter across the resource's human-readable text columns (e.g. `name`, `title`, `description`). OR-matched across those columns; omit to return everything. _(length 0–100)_ |

#### `ops_alerts_update`

**Update an alert rule**

Partial update of a rule's tunable knobs. `metricId` is immutable — the metric also pins the aggregation, so a body carrying `metricId` is rejected with `409 IMMUTABLE_FIELD`; create a new rule bound to the other metric instead (rule deletion is dashboard-only).

Pass `"notify": null` to revert the rule's delivery target back to the project default.

**Use cases**

- **Tune sensitivity** — change `threshold`/`comparator`/`windowHours` as the metric's baseline shifts.
- **Pause without losing config** — `{ "enabled": false }` instead of deleting the rule.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `name` | optional | `string` | — _(length 1–120)_ |
| `kind` | optional | `"normal" \| "anomaly" \| "outliers" \| "no_data" \| "composite"` | — |
| `comparator` | optional | `"gt" \| "gte" \| "lt" \| "lte"` | — |
| `threshold` | optional | `number` | — |
| `rangeMin` | optional | `any` | Lower edge of the corridor; `null` drops it, returning the rule to comparator and threshold when both bounds are gone. |
| `rangeMax` | optional | `any` | Upper edge of the corridor; `null` drops it. |
| `sigma` | optional | `any` | Sigmas an `anomaly` or `outliers` rule fires at; `null` restores the default of 3. |
| `direction` | optional | `any` | Which side an `anomaly` or `outliers` rule watches; `null` restores either. |
| `sustained` | optional | `boolean` | Judge the window by accumulated departure rather than bucket by bucket. `anomaly` and `outliers` only; refused alongside `requiredBuckets`. |
| `warnThreshold` | optional | `any` | The milder bound; `null` drops the warning level, leaving the rule with one. |
| `recoveryThreshold` | optional | `any` | What the metric must get back to before a live alert closes; `null` drops the hysteresis. |
| `groupAlerts` | optional | `boolean` | Fire one alert per `by()` group. Refused on a metric with no grouping. |
| `maxGroups` | optional | `any` | How many groups may alert at once; `null` restores the default of 10. |
| `noDataMinutes` | optional | `any` | How long a `no_data` rule's silence must last; `null` restores 15 minutes. |
| `delayMinutes` | optional | `any` | How far behind live the window is held; `null` drops the delay. |
| `autoResolveMinutes` | optional | `any` | Close a stale live instance after this long; `null` never auto-resolves. |
| `composite` | optional | `object` | What a `composite` rule is a boolean over. `rules` are sibling alert-rule ids in the same project and `op` is how their states combine. A child's state is what the current pass concluded about it, falling back to whether it has an open instance — so a composite still means something on a tick where a child could not be evaluated, which is exactly the tick a "two of these are broken at once" rule is for. One level deep: a child may not itself be composite. |
| `composite.op` | required | `"and" \| "or"` | How the children's states combine. |
| `composite.rules` | required | `string[]` | Ids of the alert rules to combine. Stored sorted and de-duplicated. |
| `windowHours` | optional | `integer` | — _(1–720)_ |
| `bucketMinutes` | optional | `any` | Bucket width in minutes; `null` restores the default 12 buckets per window. |
| `requiredBuckets` | optional | `any` | Buckets that must breach to fire; `null` restores "every bucket that had data". |
| `severity` | optional | `"danger" \| "warn" \| "info"` | — |
| `enabled` | optional | `boolean` | — |
| `notify` | optional | `any` | Delivery target for a rule's alert; `null` = use the project default. The `NotificationTarget` shape plus the in-app switch. |

`AGENT_NOT_CONNECTED` error sends you.

### Attachments

Screenshots, recordings, and files attached to a bug or feature request —
the evidence a QA lane captures at verification time. Upload by base64
bytes or a public https URL; append-only.

#### `ops_attachments_create`

**Attach a screenshot to an item**

Attach a screenshot, screen recording, or file to a bug or feature request, so the fixer sees what QA saw instead of reconstructing it from measurements. Send the bytes as `contentBase64` (a bare base64 string or a `data:` URI) or give a public https `url` for the server to fetch — exactly one of the two. The `kind` (`screenshot` | `recording` | `file`) defaults from the media type. Up to 25 MiB.

Error and alert tickets cannot carry attachments (`422`). Append-only: there is no replace or delete, so it is safe for restricted ops keys.

**Use case:** A QA lane captures a screenshot at verification time and the filing agent attaches it to the bug or feature request it just filed.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `contentBase64` | optional | `string` | The file bytes, base64-encoded (a bare string or a `data:<mime>;base64,` URI). Pass this or `url`, not both. |
| `url` | optional | `string` | A public https URL for the server to fetch the file from (no IP literals or internal hosts; max 25 MiB). Pass this or `contentBase64`, not both. _(format: uri)_ |
| `filename` | optional | `string` | File name, e.g. `checkout-overflow.png`. Defaults to the last segment of `url`, else `file`. |
| `mimeType` | optional | `string` | Media type, e.g. `image/png`. Defaults from the data URI, the fetched response, or the filename extension. |
| `kind` | optional | `"screenshot" \| "recording" \| "file"` | Attachment kind. Defaults from the media type (image → screenshot, video → recording, else file). Ignored by the comment-media upload. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### Comments

Comments on a queue item — the discussion thread that hangs off any bug,
feature request, or auto-filed error/alert ticket. Append a comment or read
the thread; one level of threaded replies via `parentId`.

**Mentions.** `@teammate` in a body raises an in-app notification for that
person; `@shipeasy` asks Jarvis (the AI agent) to read the item and reply.
Comments authored by Jarvis carry `authorType: system`.

#### `ops_comments_create`

**Comment on an item**

Append a comment to a queue item's thread. The body is markdown (mentions
like `@teammate` notify that person; `@shipeasy` asks Jarvis, the AI agent,
to reply). Pass `parentId` to reply under an existing top-level comment
(one level of threading — a reply to a reply attaches to the same parent).

Create-only and append-only, so it is safe for restricted ops keys — the
same channel the ops loop and Jarvis use to leave a note on an item.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `body` | required | `string` | The comment body as markdown. Mentions (`@teammate`, `@shipeasy`) are parsed from it. _(length 1–10000)_ |
| `parentId` | optional | `any` | Reply under this top-level comment. Omit / `null` for a top-level comment. Replying to a reply attaches to the same top-level parent (threading is one level deep). |
| `listToken` | optional | `string` | REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `ops_comments_list` call. It proves you listed existing ops comments and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `ops_comments_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

#### `ops_comments_list`

**List an item's comments**

List the comment thread on a queue item, oldest first. Each comment
carries its author (a teammate email, or `system` for a comment authored by
Jarvis — the AI agent), its markdown body, and `parentId` for the single
level of threaded replies. Removed comments are omitted.

**Use case:** Read the discussion on an item before replying or acting on it.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

#### `ops_comments_upload_media`

**Upload an image to embed in a comment**

Upload an image to embed in a comment on a queue item. Takes the same body as the attachment upload (`contentBase64` or `url`). The response carries a relative `url` — reference it from the comment body as a markdown image (`![caption](url)`) in `ops comments create`, so an evidence comment shows the screenshot inline.

Append-only, safe for restricted ops keys.

**Use case:** Put a screenshot inside an evidence comment rather than on the item itself.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `contentBase64` | optional | `string` | The file bytes, base64-encoded (a bare string or a `data:<mime>;base64,` URI). Pass this or `url`, not both. |
| `url` | optional | `string` | A public https URL for the server to fetch the file from (no IP literals or internal hosts; max 25 MiB). Pass this or `contentBase64`, not both. _(format: uri)_ |
| `filename` | optional | `string` | File name, e.g. `checkout-overflow.png`. Defaults to the last segment of `url`, else `file`. |
| `mimeType` | optional | `string` | Media type, e.g. `image/png`. Defaults from the data URI, the fetched response, or the filename extension. |
| `kind` | optional | `"screenshot" \| "recording" \| "file"` | Attachment kind. Defaults from the media type (image → screenshot, video → recording, else file). Ignored by the comment-media upload. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):
