### Activity

The change history of queue items — status, priority, owner and tag moves,
edits, comments, acknowledgements, and every pull-request event (linked,
unlinked, merged, closed unmerged). Read it per item or across the whole
project, filtered by kind and time, to learn what changed since a given
moment instead of diffing status lists.

#### `ops_activity_list`

**List queue activity**

The activity feed of the project's queue items, newest first: every status,
priority, owner, tag and content change, every comment, every alert
acknowledgement, and every pull-request event (`linked`, `unlinked`,
`merged`, `closed` unmerged). Each entry names the item it belongs to, who
made the change (or `github` for a merge/close the webhook observed) and
when.

Filter to one item with `item`, to one kind of change with `field`, and to a
time window with `since` / `until` (ISO-8601, exclusive). Pass
`field=pr` and `since` to learn which PRs were added to an item since you
last looked, instead of diffing status lists.

**Use case:** A QA agent polling for "what PRs were linked to item 7 since T?"
or "what changed on this project since T?".

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `item` | optional | `string` | Narrow to one item — its per-project number (e.g. `7`) or full id. Omit for the whole project. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `field` | optional | `"status" \| "priority" \| "owner" \| "tags" \| "ack" \| "pr" \| "comment" \| "edit"` | Which kind of change an activity entry records. `pr` is a pull-request event (see `pr.event`); `comment` carries an excerpt in `to`; `edit` names the edited content fields in `added`. |
| `since` | optional | `string` | Only entries strictly after this ISO-8601 instant. _(format: date-time)_ |
| `until` | optional | `string` | Only entries strictly before this ISO-8601 instant. _(format: date-time)_ |
| `limit` | optional | `integer` | Maximum entries to return (1-200). Defaults to 100. _(1–200)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).

### Memory

Project memory — what the project learned from every ticket it shipped or
declined: decisions from answered questions, QA findings, the files each
feature lives in, and the PR that shipped it. Derived from the tickets'
own records and rebuilt when they change. Search it before you start a
ticket so you build on what was decided instead of rediscovering it.

#### `ops_memory_search`

**Search project memory**

What the project already learned from the tickets it shipped — the
decisions the team made in answered questions, what QA found, which files
a feature lives in, the PR that shipped it, and the requests that were
turned down. Every entry is derived from the item's own records
(investigations, questions, QA notes, linked PRs) and is rebuilt whenever
those change, so it never disagrees with the ticket.

Search with `q` (free text), `paths` (comma-separated files or
directories — entries that touched them rank first), `item` (a queue
item — its title and description become the query, and its own entries
are left out) or `trail` (a trail — its title, intent and goal become the
query; its own and its items' entries are left out). With none of them, the newest entries come back. Bodies are
capped; read the full ticket with `ops get <item>`.

**Use case:** A coding agent picks up a ticket and, before reading the
repo, asks what was already decided and built around it:
`ops memory search --item 42`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | optional | `string` | Free-text query, e.g. `checkout retry`. _(length 1–500)_ |
| `paths` | optional | `string` | Comma-separated repo-relative files or directories, e.g. `apps/web/src/checkout/,packages/billing/src/retry.ts`. _(length 1–2000)_ |
| `item` | optional | `string` | A queue item — its per-project number (e.g. `7`) or full id. Its title and description become the query; its own entries are excluded. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `trail` | optional | `string` | A trail — its handle (e.g. `T-12`) or full id. Its title, intent and goal become the query; its own entries and its items' are excluded. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `kind` | optional | `"shipped" \| "declined" \| "decision" \| "qa" \| "outcome"` | What a project-memory entry records. `shipped` — an item that reached `ready_for_qa`/`resolved`: what was asked, what the run found, the files it touched, the PR. `declined` — an item closed `wont_fix`: the request and why it was turned down. `decision` — an answered structured question: what the team picked. `qa` — a QA note or an answered QA question: what "fixed" turned out to mean, or what QA found failing. `outcome` — what a trail's plan achieved against its goal metric: what was tried, the reading, met or missed. A trail's own `decision` entries are its answered questions and its approved plan revisions. |
| `limit` | optional | `integer` | Maximum entries to return (1-50). Defaults to 10. _(1–50)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

### Brain

The project brain — a knowledge graph of notes and typed links that grows
on its own from the work (every item, trail, PR, file, flag and metric is
a note, linked the moment anything mentions it) and from knowledge sent
in, which is reconciled into what is already known: later and stronger
sources rewrite weaker or older ones, and every rewrite keeps a revision.
Search it before you design; teach it what you learned.

#### `ops_brain_coverage`

**Check how complete the brain is on a topic**

What the brain knows about a topic, and what it is missing, as a ranked
worklist. It takes the notes matching `topic` (or `slug` and its
neighbours), then checks them for gaps: subjects other notes link to that
nobody wrote, thin notes, notes with no summary, notes that name code but
are not grounded in it, anchors whose code changed, held claims, live
contradictions, notes untouched for six months, and the kinds of
knowledge still missing (no pitfall, no decision…). `score` is 0-100.
`next` is what to write, worst first.

**Use case:** a system keeps the brain complete on what matters. It reads
`ops brain coverage --topic checkout`, ingests notes that answer `next`,
and reads coverage again until the score stops moving.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `topic` | optional | `string` | The subject to check, e.g. `checkout retries`. Pass this or `slug`; with neither, the whole brain is checked (its newest 300 notes). _(length 1–500)_ |
| `slug` | optional | `string` | Check a note and its neighbourhood instead of a search. _(length 1–300)_ |
| `depth` | optional | `integer` | Hops around the matches to include (0-2). Defaults to 1. _(0–2)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

#### `ops_brain_get`

**Read one brain note**

One note in full: body, current facts and their history, held claims,
every source that asserted it, and every link in and out (a backlink
reads by its inverse relation — `touched_by`, `superseded_by`).

**Use case:** `ops brain get flag/checkout` shows every item, trail,
decision and pitfall that mentions the flag.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slug` | required | `string` | The note's slug: `flag/checkout`, `item/42`, `file/apps/web/src/a.ts`, `checkout-retry-policy`. _(length 1–300)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

#### `ops_brain_graph`

**Read a neighbourhood of the brain**

The notes within `depth` hops of `slug` (links followed both ways) and the
edges between them — or, without a slug, the most recently updated notes
and their edges.

**Use case:** Everything two hops from `item/42`: its files, the flags it
mentions, and the pitfalls other work left on them.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `slug` | optional | `string` | The note to start from. _(length 1–300)_ |
| `depth` | optional | `integer` | Hops to follow (1-4). Defaults to 2. _(1–4)_ |
| `limit` | optional | `integer` | Maximum notes (1-300). Defaults to 100. _(1–300)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

#### `ops_brain_ingest`

**Teach the brain**

Send knowledge in — one to twenty notes. Each is reconciled into the note
its title lands on rather than added beside it: the later claim wins
within the same source strength, a weaker source never overwrites a
stronger one (a person > verified code > a merged PR > a ticket > text
sent in), every rewrite keeps a revision, and the same text twice changes
nothing.

By default shipeasy's model extracts and verifies the text (billed to the
project's Jarvis credits). When you already wrote each note in its final
form — seeding from the repo — pass `extract: false` and use the markup:
`type:: convention`, `summary:: one line`, `key:: value` facts, typed
links (`depends_on:: [[Billing]]`), `[[Other note]]`, `@gate:<key>`, `#42`,
backticked repo paths. Ground each note with `evidence` — a repo path and
a snippet copied verbatim from it; verified evidence makes the note
outrank anything said about that code, and it is re-checked when the file
changes. Tag a note with the project's own tags: `tags:: checkout, ios`
(see `tags list`). Only tags the project already has are kept; any other
comes back in `dropped`. Lessons, not logs: one subject per note.

**Use case:** Seeding: read README / CLAUDE.md / design docs, then send
`{notes: [{text: "# Retries are capped\ntype:: convention\n…", extract: false, source: "seed:claude", evidence: [{path: "src/retry.ts", snippet: "export const MAX_RETRIES = 3;"}]}]}`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `notes` | required | `object[]` | One to twenty notes, each reconciled into the note its title lands on. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

#### `ops_brain_search`

**Search the project brain**

Search the project's knowledge graph — conventions, pitfalls, decisions,
concepts and facts, plus a note for every item, trail, flag, metric, PR
and file they link. Title and slug hits rank over body hits, and a
well-linked note over a lonely one. No `q` returns the most recently
updated notes. Read one in full with `ops brain get <slug>`.

**Use case:** Before designing a change to checkout, an agent asks what
the team knows: `ops brain search "checkout retry"`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `q` | optional | `string` | Free-text query, e.g. `checkout retry`. _(length 1–500)_ |
| `type` | optional | `"item" \| "trail" \| "flag" \| "experiment" \| "config" \| "killswitch" \| "metric" \| "universe" \| "alert" \| "pr" \| "file" \| "concept" \| "decision" \| "convention" \| "pitfall" \| "fact"` | A note's type. Entity notes (`item` … `file`) mirror something that exists elsewhere and are created the first time anything links to them; knowledge notes (`concept`, `decision`, `convention`, `pitfall`, `fact`) hold what the team learned. |
| `limit` | optional | `integer` | Maximum notes to return (1-100). Defaults to 20. _(1–100)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).

#### `ops_brain_sources`

**List what the brain read**

The brain's intake: every input it read (text sent in, shipped items,
answered questions, trails), newest first, with its extraction state,
the notes it produced and the model tokens it cost.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `limit` | optional | `integer` | Maximum sources (1-200). Defaults to 50. _(1–200)_ |

#### `ops_brain_status`

**Brain status and seeding guide**

What the project brain holds — notes per type, links, candidates, held
claims, orphans, the intake queue — and `guide`, the playbook for seeding
or extending it. Call it first when asked to set up, seed or grow the
brain, and again when done to report what changed.

**Use case:** "Set up our brain" — read the status, follow `guide`
(read the repo's own knowledge, write notes with `ops brain ingest`), then
read the status again.

_Parameters_

_No parameters._

### Investigations

Investigation records on a queue item — the structured, read-only write-ups
an AI agent produces while working it (findings / a blocking question / QA
notes), plus the `working` run rows an ack or an AI hand-off opens. This is
the AI-write seam the cockpit's detail panel renders: `list` reads what a
previous run found, `create` appends a new record, and `update` fills in the
`working` run record you were handed (findings, PR, confidence) as you work.

#### `ops_investigations_create`

**Record an investigation**

Append one structured investigation record to a queue item — the AI-write
seam the cockpit's detail panel renders read-only. Post your findings
(`kind: investigated`), a blocking question for the team (`kind: question`), or how to verify the fix (`kind: ready_for_qa` with
`qaNotes`). Append-only and create-only, so it is safe for restricted ops
keys. For a decision between options you can name, ask a structured
question instead (`ops questions ask`) — it is answerable in one tap and
the answer comes back to your run.

**Use case:** After working an item, leave a findings write-up (summary,
markdown findings, sources inspected, confidence) so the team — and the
next agent run — sees what you learned.

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `kind` | required | `"investigated" \| "detected" \| "question" \| "ready_for_qa" \| "working" \| "note"` | Which lifecycle stage the record documents. |
| `summary` | optional | `string` | One-line summary of the record. _(length 0–2000)_ |
| `findings` | optional | `string` | The full findings write-up (markdown). _(length 0–50000)_ |
| `question` | optional | `string` | A blocking question for the team (markdown). _(length 0–10000)_ |
| `qaNotes` | optional | `string` | How to verify the fix — QA notes (markdown). _(length 0–50000)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | The agent type producing the record — pass your own type when you are a coding agent. |
| `model` | optional | `string` | The model the agent ran on. _(length 0–200)_ |
| `connectorId` | optional | `string` | The trigger-connector row id the agent ran through. _(length 0–200)_ |
| `prNumber` | optional | `integer` | A PR the record references. |
| `prUrl` | optional | `string` | HTML URL of that PR. _(length 0–2000; format: uri)_ |

| `durationMs` | optional | `integer` | Run duration in milliseconds. |
| `visibility` | optional | `"draft" \| "published"` | Record visibility. Defaults to `published`; `draft` keeps it out of the panel. |

It proves you listed existing ops investigations and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `ops_investigations_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

### Questions

Structured questions an agent asks the team about a queue item — the
`AskUserQuestion` shape: a short `header`, the `question`, 2–4 `options`
(label + description), and `multiSelect` for checkboxes instead of radios.
Every question also accepts a free-text "Other" answer. Open questions sit
at the very top of the item's detail panel and mark the row in the queue.

**Asking.** `ask` posts 1–4 questions at once. Several agents (or several
runs) may have questions open on the same item at the same time.

**Getting the answer back.** `delivery: resume` (the default for a run
launched through a trigger connector) re-fires that same agent on the
item once every question its run asked is answered, continuing the same
run record with the answers in the prompt. `delivery: poll` (the default
for a live, connector-less session such as Claude Code in a terminal)
fires nothing — call `list` until the status reads `completed`.

#### `ops_questions_answer`

**Answer a question**

Answer one open question on a queue item — pick option labels in
`selected` (exactly one unless the question is `multiSelect`) and/or
write a free-text `other`. The question moves to `completed`. When it was
the last open question of a `resume` run, that agent is re-fired on the
item with every answer. A person's action: never allow-listed for
restricted ops keys.

**Use case:** Unblock an agent from the CLI instead of the dashboard.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |

| `selected` | optional | `string[]` | The option labels picked — exactly one for a single-select question (unless answering only with `other`), one or more for `multiSelect`. |

#### `ops_questions_ask`

**Ask the team questions about an item**

Ask 1–4 structured questions about a queue item — the way to get a
decision from a person when the implementation needs one. Each question
is the `AskUserQuestion` shape: a short `header` chip, the full
`question`, 2–4 `options` (`label` + `description`), and `multiSelect`
(checkboxes instead of radios). The person can always answer "Other" in
free text, or "No preference" (leave the call to you — take the simplest,
least-change option), so never add an "Other" or a "No preference"
option yourself. The questions render
at the very top of the item's detail panel and mark the row in the queue.

**Delivery.** `resume` re-fires your trigger-connector run on the item
once every question it asked is answered, continuing the same run record
with the answers in the prompt — stop after asking. `poll` fires nothing;
poll `GET .../questions` instead. Omitted, it is `resume` when `runId`
names a run launched through a trigger connector, else `poll`.

**On a trail.** Pass the trail handle (`T-12`) as `handle` and the plan
run's id as `runId`: a plan run asks how the trail should ship this way,
and a `resume` answer re-fires the same plan run with the answers in its
prompt. The questions render in the trail page's Plan section.

**Use case:** Blocked on a product decision (which behaviour to keep,
which of two fixes to ship) — ask instead of guessing, then wait for the
answer.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `questions` | required | `object[]` | 1–4 questions to ask at once. |
| `runId` | optional | `string` | The run (investigation record id) you are working the item under — the `runId` an ack or a launch handed you. Ties the questions to that run so a `resume` delivery continues it. _(length 0–200)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | The agent type asking — pass your own type when you are a coding agent. Defaults to the run's agent. |
| `delivery` | optional | `"resume" \| "poll"` | How the answer gets back to the asker — `resume` re-fires the asking run's trigger connector on the item once every question that run asked is answered; `poll` fires nothing and the asker reads `GET .../questions`. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

#### `ops_questions_cancel`

**Withdraw a question**

Withdraw one open question you asked — it no longer needs an answer
(you found it out yourself, or the item moved on). The question moves to
`cancelled` and leaves the detail panel. Withdrawing the last open
question of a run delivers nothing.

**Use case:** You asked, then answered it yourself from the code — take

#### `ops_questions_list`

**List an item's questions**

The structured questions asked on a queue item, with their answers —
newest first (max 100). Pull this to read the answers to questions you
asked: an answered question reads `status: completed` and carries
`answer.selected` (the option labels picked) and `answer.other` (the
free-text "Other" reply, or `null`). `answer.selected` of exactly
`["No preference"]` means the person has no opinion: pick the simplest

**Use case:** You asked with `delivery: poll` from a live session — poll

### Checklist

The to-do checklist inside a feature or bug item — the things being
implemented, kept in the item's body instead of in comments. The dev (or a
coding agent) adds lines and ticks them `done` as they land; QA marks each
done line `verified`, or `returned` with a note that says what is still
wrong, which hands it back to the dev. `ops get` carries the list as
`checklist`, so an agent reads its work order with the item.

#### `ops_checklist_add`

**Add a checklist line**

Add one line to the end of a queue item's checklist, `open`. Write a
multi-part plan as one line per part, so the dev can tick each off and QA
can verify or return each on its own. The author is the caller's identity;
pass `agent` to record the line as added by that agent type. An item holds
at most 200 lines.

**Use case:** An agent starting a feature lists the four changes it will
make, then ticks them off as they land.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `text` | required | `string` | What the line asks for (markdown, one line). _(length 1–500)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | The agent type adding the line — pass your own type when you are a coding agent. Omitted, the line is attributed to the caller's identity. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

#### `ops_checklist_update`

**Update a checklist line**

Change one checklist line: its `text`, its `position`, or its `status`.
The dev ticks a line `done` (or back to `open`); QA marks a `done` line
`verified`, or `returned` with a `note` saying what is still wrong; ticking
a returned line `done` again clears the note and hands it back to QA. Who
did what is recorded from the caller's identity, or `agent` when given. An
illegal move (verifying an `open` line) answers 409 `INVALID_TRANSITION`.

**Use case:** QA retests a feature, verifies three lines and returns the
fourth: "the export still drops the header row".

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `itemId` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `text` | optional | `string` | New text for the line. _(length 1–500)_ |
| `status` | optional | `"open" \| "done" \| "verified" \| "returned"` | Where a checklist line stands — `open` (still to do), `done` (the dev ticked it), `verified` (QA confirmed it) or `returned` (QA sent it back with a `note`; tick it `done` again once fixed). |
| `note` | optional | `string` | Why QA returns the line — required when moving it to `returned` (send it alone to reword the note of a returned line), refused on a line that ends up in any other status. _(length 1–2000)_ |
| `position` | optional | `integer` | New display position (lines sort ascending; ties by creation order). _(≥ 0)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | The agent type making the change — pass your own type when you are an agent. Omitted, the change is attributed to the caller's identity. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### Trigger

Recurring coding-agent triggers: the scheduled, unattended runs that burn
down the ops queue in `--pr` mode (one PR per fixed item; nothing
auto-merges). Shipeasy can fire four providers directly — Claude routines,
Cursor cloud agents, Copilot cloud agents, and Google Jules (the Gemini
path) — registered here as trigger connectors (idempotent per provider
key). Other platforms (Codex, Windsurf, Cline, OpenClaw, OpenCode,
Continue) schedule on their own surface — typically a GitHub Actions
`schedule:` cron running the platform's headless CLI with the shared
trigger prompt.

#### `ops_trigger_create_claude`

Register a Claude Code scheduled routine as the trigger connector. Creates (or idempotently updates) a coding-agent **trigger** connector — the recurring, unattended run that burns down the ops queue in `--pr` mode. Discriminated on `provider`; only the four Shipeasy-fireable providers are accepted (`claude_trigger`, `cursor_trigger`, `copilo…

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| `events` | optional | `"bug.created" \| "feature_request.created"[]` | Events that auto-fire the routine. Defaults to empty so the trigger does not auto-fire paid runs until events are subscribed. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `config` | required | `object` | Non-secret config for a Claude trigger. |
| `config.routineId` | required | `string` | The Claude Code routine id this connector fires (the id recorded at setup). Idempotency key for the connector. _(length 1–∞)_ |
| `config.fireText` | optional | `string` | Optional default prompt sent on a manual fire / when no event text applies. _(length 1–∞)_ |
| `token` | optional | `string` | The routine's fire bearer token (secret). **Optional** — a tokenless trigger is recorded but not fireable until a token is added later. Encrypted into the credentials cipher; never persisted in `config` or returned. _(length 1–∞)_ |
| `enabled` | optional | `boolean` | Whether the trigger is active on create. _(default `true`)_ |

## Trails

Trails: the unit of shipping, from intent through merge to release. A trail
is created on purpose — from scratch, or with **Ship this** on a queue item
— and holds what was asked for (a title and a body with the outcome and the
acceptance criteria), every pull request worked under it (each a *change*),
the queue items discovered while it was worked, reviewed or released, and
the flags, kill switches, experiments, metrics, alert rules and i18n keys
it ships. It replaces the pull request as the thing that is reviewed and
merged, and it owns the decision to release.

**Loop.** Start a coding agent on the trail (`start`). It opens pull
requests and links them (`link-pr`). Every push to a change is scored by
the project's review agents (a value, a rationale and findings per agent);
merge gates read branch freshness, approvals, open findings, blocking evals,
CI checks, discovered items and the release gates into one verdict. When a
change fails, the server re-fires the coding agent with the findings, up to
the gates' `fixRounds`. Findings that are real but out of scope are promoted
to queue items (`promote-finding`) rather than fixed in passing.

**Phase.** `planning`, `building`, `reviewing`, `ready`, `releasing`,
`shipped`, `closed`. After the last open change merges the trail is
`releasing` until its flags are fully rolled out and its experiments decided.

**Handles.** A trail is addressed by its per-project handle (`T-12`) or its
id. A queue item belongs to at most one trail.

**Approve and merge are a person's call.** They are accepted only from a
dashboard session or a device-auth CLI session, and are not exposed as MCP
tools.

The v1 item routes (`/api/admin/ops/{handle}/trail/...`) remain as aliases
that resolve the item's trail and answer `404` when it has none.

### `trails_attribute`

**Attribute an item to a trail**

Record that an error, alert or bug was caused by the trail after it merged. Errors carry no release or commit SHA, so attribution is a judgement: compare the stack frames and the error's subject against each candidate trail's changed files (`trails get --files`) and resources, and attribute only on concrete evidence — a frame in a changed file, the failing call touching a resource of the trail, or a guard metric of the trail. If nothing fits, leave the item unattributed.

- `confidence: high` or `medium` puts the item on the trail with source `post_merge`, and writes `evidence` as an investigation note on the item and a system comment on the trail.
- `confidence: low` records a *suspect* instead: the trail lists it under suspected regressions and a person confirms or rejects it.

Attribution never flips a rollback. Propose one to a person as a structured question.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** A new error's stack frame sits in a file T-12 changed two hours ago; the investigating agent attributes it with the frame as evidence.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `item` | required | `string` | The error, alert or bug to attribute (number or id). _(length 1–64)_ |
| `confidence` | required | `"high" \| "medium" \| "low"` | How sure an attribution is. `high` and `medium` attach the item to the trail; `low` records a suspect for a person to confirm or reject. |
| `evidence` | required | `string` | Concrete evidence: a stack frame in a changed file, the failing call touching a resource of the trail, or a guard metric of the trail. _(length 1–4000)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.
- `REFERENCED_NOT_FOUND` — A referenced entity (universe, metric, gate, event) does not exist.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_close`

**Close a trail**

Close a trail by hand — abandoned, superseded, or shipped with discovered items still open. A trail also closes on its own once it is `shipped` with no discovered item open at `high` priority or above. Closing never merges or closes pull requests. A trail closed with nothing merged reads `closed`; one that merged keeps its `releasing`/`shipped` phase.

Closing is a person's call: the restricted ops key cannot close a trail.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `reason` | optional | `string` | Why the trail is being closed, e.g. `abandoned` or `superseded by T-14`. _(length 0–2000)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_confirm_suspect`

**Confirm a suspected regression**

Confirm a suspect: the item goes onto the trail with source `post_merge` and the suspect's evidence is kept. A person's call — the restricted ops key cannot confirm.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `suspectId` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.

### `trails_create`

**Create a trail**

Creates a trail in `planning`. A trail is created on purpose — nothing makes one implicitly. Create one from scratch with a `title` and a `body` (the outcome and the acceptance criteria), or press **Ship this** on a queue item with `originItem`: the item's description seeds the body and the item becomes the trail's first item, with source `origin`. An item is on at most one trail.

A trail may carry a `goal` (the metric it is meant to move, with a baseline and a target), a `startDate` and a `targetDate`, and a `health` set by hand (omitted, it is derived).

Fire the project's coding agent on the new trail with `trails start`, or link pull requests an agent already opened with `trails link-pr`.

**Autopilot.** `autopilot: { enabled: true, limits }` turns on autopilot at creation: the plan's questions are answered with the agent's recommendation, the plan is approved, and the change merges when every blocking gate is green, all inside the limits. It needs the `autopilot` capability and a person's identity (a dashboard session or a signed-in CLI); an ops key, an admin key or MCP asking for it is refused with `403`. Everything else is safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** A coding agent that was asked to ship a multi-part feature opens one trail for it, then links every PR it opens.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `title` | required | `string` | One-line statement of the intent. _(length 1–200; pattern `^\S(.*\S)?$`)_ |
| `body` | optional | `string` | The intent in markdown — the outcome and the acceptance criteria. _(default `""`; length 0–20000)_ |
| `type` | optional | `"feature" \| "bug" \| "task"` | What a trail is shipping. A `feature` trail is held to the rollback and measured release gates. |
| `priority` | optional | `any` | Initial triage priority, or `null`. |
| `ownerId` | optional | `any` | The `users.id` of the person to own the trail, or `null`. |
| `ownerConnectorId` | optional | `any` | The agent connector to own the trail, or `null`. |
| `repos` | optional | `string[]` | Repos (`owner/repo`) the trail may open changes in. _(default `[]`)_ |
| `originItem` | optional | `string` | Ship this: a queue item (number or id) to create the trail from. Its description seeds `body` when that is omitted, and it becomes the trail's first item with source `origin`. _(length 1–64)_ |
| `startDate` | optional | `any` | The calendar day work starts (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or `null`. |
| `targetDate` | optional | `any` | The calendar day the trail is meant to ship by (`YYYY-MM-DD`), or `null`. |
| `health` | optional | `any` | A health a person sets, or `null` (the default) to have it derived. |
| `goal` | optional | `any` | The metric the trail is meant to move, or `null` for none. |
| `intake` | optional | `object` | What the creation dialog already decided — each field is a plan question answered in advance. The plan run asks only what is left out. Omitted entirely, the plan asks everything ("let the plan ask me"). |
| `intake.requirePlan` | optional | `boolean` | A person approves the plan before it builds, for this trail. Omitted, the project's setting (`trail-gates` `requirePlan`). |
| `intake.strategy` | optional | `"straight_to_main" \| "flag" \| "flag_experiment" \| "kill_switch" \| "flag_kill_switch" \| "other"` | How the trail ships, as the person chose it while the plan was made — `straight_to_main` (no flag), `flag`, `flag_experiment` (a flag measured by an experiment), `kill_switch` (a kill switch only), `flag_kill_switch`, or `other` (a free-text answer that fits none of those). |
| `intake.flagKey` | optional | `string` | The flag's key, when the person named one. _(length 1–200)_ |
| `intake.rollout` | optional | `object` | How the flag a trail ships behind is ramped after merge — the release controller's plan (see the design doc, the release controller). Part of the plan's release block; the project's defaults live in `trail-gates` `rollout`. The controller runs on the alerts cron, so a hold shorter than the cron interval rounds up to the next tick. |
| `intake.rollout.steps` | required | `number[]` | Percent steps, each above the one before, the last 100. |
| `intake.rollout.holdMinutes` | required | `integer` | Minutes a step must stay healthy before the next one. _(0–10080)_ |
| `intake.rollout.minExposure` | required | `integer` | Evaluations a step must have served before it counts as healthy, so a quiet hour never passes as a green one. `0` = no floor. _(≥ 0)_ |
| `intake.rollout.internal` | optional | `any` | The team stage before any public percent — the project's members are allowlisted on the flag (by email) and the step holds like any other. `null` or absent = no team stage. |
| `intake.rollout.guards` | required | `object` | What is watched while a step holds. The trail's `guards` alert-rule resources are watched too. |
| `intake.rollout.guards.alertRuleIds` | required | `string[]` | Alert rules (ids) whose firing during a step is a breach. |
| `intake.rollout.guards.experimentGuardrails` | required | `boolean` | Whether a breached guardrail of the trail's measuring experiment is a breach. |
| `intake.rollout.guards.attributedErrors` | required | `boolean` | Whether a new error attributed to the trail at high confidence is a breach. |
| `intake.rollout.policies` | required | `object` | The three rollout decisions — the project defaults unless the creation dialog or a plan edit sets them. |
| `intake.rollout.policies.onBreach` | required | `"pull_back" \| "ask_first" \| "ask_then_pull_back"` | What to do when a guard trips during a step — `pull_back` (pull the flag back, investigate and suggest a fix, tell the owner; the default), `ask_first` (ask the owner, only notify), or `ask_then_pull_back` (ask, and pull back after `breachTimeoutMinutes` with no answer). |
| `intake.rollout.policies.breachTimeoutMinutes` | required | `integer` | With `ask_then_pull_back`, minutes the owner has before the controller pulls back. _(1–1440)_ |
| `intake.rollout.policies.advance` | required | `"auto" \| "ask"` | Whether a healthy step advances by itself (`auto`) or waits for the owner to say so (`ask`). |
| `intake.rollout.policies.afterFix` | required | `"resume" \| "ask" \| "restart"` | What happens when the fix merges — `resume` from the last healthy step, `ask` the owner first, or `restart` from the first step. |
| `autopilot` | optional | `object` | Turn a trail's autopilot on or off, and set the limits it acts inside. Turning it ON needs the `autopilot` capability (admins have it) and a person's identity — a dashboard session or a signed-in CLI, never an ops key, an admin key or MCP — and makes that person the accountable approver. Turning it off is open to the trail's owner, whoever authorized it, and admins. |
| `autopilot.enabled` | required | `boolean` | Whether autopilot is on. |
| `autopilot.limits` | optional | `object` | Limits to set; each one omitted keeps the trail's current value (the project's default for a new trail). |
| `autopilot.limits.maxRisk` | optional | `any` | — |
| `autopilot.limits.repos` | optional | `string[]` | — |
| `autopilot.limits.types` | optional | `"feature" \| "bug" \| "task"[]` | — |
| `autopilot.limits.maxFixRounds` | optional | `integer` | — _(0–10)_ |
| `autopilot.limits.maxPullBacks` | optional | `integer` | — _(0–10)_ |
| `autopilot.limits.maxRuns` | optional | `integer` | — _(0–100)_ |
| `listToken` | optional | `string` | REQUIRED. The `listToken` returned by the most recent `trails_list` call. It proves you listed existing trails and confirmed this one doesn't already exist before creating it. Call `trails_list` first if you don't have a fresh token. |

### `trails_get`

**Show a trail**

A trail followed from intent to release: its phase, every change (each a pull request) with its latest push, merge gates, CI checks, each review agent's eval next to its last five, every finding (open first, worst first, `stale` when raised on an earlier push), approvals and pushes; the items discovered on it; the product resources it ships with their live state; the runs working it; and the suspected regressions awaiting a person.

Gates are read live from GitHub on every call, so a `state` of `unknown` means GitHub could not be read and the PR-backed gates read `pending`. Phase and counts are recomputed live. Pass `files` to include each merged change's full changed-file list and the diff link.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** After pushing a fix, a coding agent reads the trail to see which findings are still open and whether the scores have turned green.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `files` | optional | `boolean` | Include each merged change's full `changedFiles` list. Omitted, `changedFiles` is `null`. _(default `false`)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

### `trails_link_pr`

**Link a pull request to a trail**

Link a pull request to the trail as one of its *changes*. From then on the GitHub webhook records its pushes, the project's review agents score each push, and the merge gates read it. Linking a pull request the trail already has is a no-op; a pull request that belongs to a different trail is refused with `409`. Pass `item` when an item's run opened the PR, so the change shows under that item.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** A coding agent working a trail opens a PR and links it with `trails link-pr T-12 <url>`.

| `prUrl` | required | `string` | The pull request's URL. _(length 1–500)_ |
| `item` | optional | `string` | The queue item whose run opened the PR (number or id), when there is one. Omitted, the change belongs to the trail itself. _(length 1–64)_ |

### `trails_list`

**List trails**

Returns the project's trails, newest activity first. A trail is the unit of shipping: an outcome that takes several items, pull requests and release tools, with a lead, start and target dates, a health and a progress (items done over items on the trail). The phase, health and counts on each row are a snapshot; read one trail with `trails get` for the live state.

**Dashboard table read.** `view=table` is the contract every dashboard list table shares: the endpoint applies `f`, `sort` and `cursor` in SQL and answers `{ data, next_cursor, section_counts?, grouped? }`. Filters and sorts are never applied in the browser, so a condition the server cannot evaluate is a `400`.
- `f` — a JSON array of `{ "f": field, "o": operator, "v": value }` conditions, all ANDed. Fields are the snapshot columns: `phase`, `status`, `type`, `priority`, `owner`, `health`, `targetDate`, `changesOpen`, `changesMergeable`, `findingsOpenHigh`, `itemsOpen`, `itemsTotal`, `itemsDone`, `releasedPct`, `updatedAt`.
- `sort` — a column id, `-` prefixed for descending: `number`, `title`, `phase`, `priority`, `owner`, `health`, `progress` (items done over items on the trail), `target` (the target date), `changes`, `findings`, `items`, `released`, `updated`, `created`. Defaults to `-updated`.
- `cursor` — the previous page's `next_cursor`; `limit` is the page size (1–200, default 50).

**Scopes** (`scope`) are the dashboard's tabs: `mine` (trails you own), `reviewing`, `ready`, `releasing`, `shipped`, `closed`, or `all` (the default).

**Attribution.** `mergedSince` and `touches` list the trails that merged inside a window and changed a path or linked a resource — the candidates for an error or alert that started after a release.

**Use case:** Find the trail already shipping a feature before creating another, or list what merged in the last 72 hours to attribute a new alert.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `view` | optional | `"table"` | `table` answers the dashboard table read (`f`, `sort`, `cursor`, `limit`, `section_counts`, `grouped`). Omitted, `f` and `sort` are still honoured and the envelope is `{ data, next_cursor }`. |
| `scope` | optional | `"all" \| "mine" \| "reviewing" \| "ready" \| "releasing" \| "shipped" \| "closed"` | A dashboard tab: `mine` (owned by the caller), `reviewing`, `ready`, `releasing`, `shipped`, `closed`, or `all` (the default, no narrowing). _(default `"all"`)_ |
| `phase` | optional | `"planning" \| "building" \| "reviewing" \| "ready" \| "releasing" \| "shipped" \| "closed"` | Where a trail is, derived from its changes and its release resources — `planning` (no change and no open run), `building` (no change yet, a run is working), `reviewing` (a change is open and not every open change can merge), `ready` (every open change can merge), `releasing` (merged, and a flag, experiment or other release resource has not settled), `shipped` (merged and every release resource settled), `closed` (closed with nothing merged). The detail read recomputes it live; the list reads a snapshot. |
| `type` | optional | `"feature" \| "bug" \| "task"` | What a trail is shipping. A `feature` trail is held to the rollback and measured release gates. |
| `health` | optional | `"on_track" \| "at_risk" \| "off_track"` | A trail's effective health — the one a person set, or else the derived one. Derived, first match wins: `off_track` when the target date has passed and the trail has not shipped, or a rollout is `fixing` after a pull-back; `at_risk` when the target is at most 7 days away and progress is under 75 %, or a high finding or a high or critical item on the trail is open; otherwise `on_track`. A list row carries the snapshot; the detail read recomputes it. |
| `owner` | optional | `string` | Narrow to trails owned by one person OR one agent — a `users.id`, email or display name, or a connector id, display name or handle. Case-insensitive exact match. |
| `q` | optional | `string` | Case-insensitive substring filter across the trail's title and body. _(length 0–100)_ |
| `mergedSince` | optional | `string` | ISO-8601 timestamp. Narrow to trails with a change merged at or after it. _(format: date-time)_ |
| `touches` | optional | `string` | A file path (or path prefix) a merged change changed, or a resource key the trail links. Narrow to trails that touch it. _(length 0–500)_ |
| `f` | optional | `string` | The table's filter conditions: a JSON array of `{ "f", "o", "v" }` objects, ANDed. See the operation description for the fields. _(length 0–8000)_ |
| `sort` | optional | `string` | A column id, `-` prefixed for descending (`-updated`). An unknown column is a `400`. _(length 0–32)_ |
| `cursor` | optional | `string` | Opaque cursor returned in the previous page's `next_cursor`. Omit for the first page. |
| `limit` | required | `integer` | Page size (1–200). A page shorter than `limit` is the last one. _(1–200)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_pause_rollout`

**Pause a trail's rollout**

Pause the release controller on a trail: it stops stepping the flag and watching the guards until the rollout is resumed. The flag stays wherever it is. A trail that ships behind several flags has a rollout per flag; pass `resource` (the flag's trail-resource id or its key) to pause one, or omit it to pause every flag. Any manual change to the flag pauses the controller the same way, so a person and the controller never fight over it. Safe to call at any time; pausing a rollout that is not running answers `409`.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** The checkout flag is at 25% and a deploy is going out; hold the ramp until it is done.

### `trails_promote_finding`

**Promote a finding to a queue item**

Move a finding that is real but out of scope onto the queue. It creates a bug (or a feature request, with `type`) whose description quotes the finding, its path and line, and its push. ### `trails_release_facts`

**Read a trail's release facts**

What the numbers say about how the trail can ship, before anyone picks an approach: the traffic reaching the surface (distinct units a day over the last 28 days), its tier, whether a 50/50 experiment would reach significance within 28 days at the lift the goal asks for (or 5%), what 28 days could detect, and a rollout sized to the traffic — a team stage, then steps coarse where 1% would be a handful of people, holds long enough for a step to see its minimum exposure.

The traffic is read from `proxy` when given (`metric:<key>`, `event:<name>` or `flag:<key>`), else the trail's goal metric, else a flag already on the trail. With nothing to read the tier is `none` — pass an event on the surface the trail changes.

The plan run reads these before it asks how to ship, and `submit-plan` checks the plan against them. Read-only. Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** A plan run on "redesign the onboarding checklist" passes `proxy=event:onboarding_viewed`, learns it is 120 users a day and that an experiment would need 90 days, and recommends a flag with guards instead.

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `proxy` | optional | `string` | What to read the traffic from — `metric:<key>`, `event:<name>` or `flag:<key>`. _(length 0–220; pattern `^(metric\|event\|flag):.+$`)_ |

### `trails_start`

**Start an agent on a trail**

Fire the project's coding-agent trigger on the trail. While the trail has no approved plan, this fires a read-only **plan** run: it reads the trail, works out what would reach the goal, asks the person only what the goal leaves open (which approach, the scope) through `ops questions ask`, chooses how it ships (straight to main, behind a flag, flag and experiment, kill switch, flag and kill switch) itself from the release facts, then submits a plan with `trails submit-plan`. Once the plan is approved (`trails approve-plan`), starting an agent **builds** it. Where the project turned plan approval off (`trail-gates` `requirePlan`), the plan run asks nothing and a plan with no warnings approves itself and starts the build.

**Build.** When the approved plan filed items, `build` launches an item run for every open item of the first milestone that still has open items and no run working it (items without a milestone count as the first), at most `trail-gates` `maxParallelRuns` (default 3) at once, and no trail-level build run: `run` is `null` and `itemRuns` says what happened to each item. Each item run opens its own pull request, which becomes a change of the trail. Otherwise one trail-level build run carries the plan to pull requests, creates exactly the resources the plan lists and links them, as before, and `itemRuns` is empty.

**Replan.** Once a plan is approved, `kind: replan` fires a read-only run that re-reads the goal metric, the items' outcomes and project memory and submits the plan's next revision, which waits as `drafted` for approval.

`fix` runs are fired by the server when a change's evals or findings fail. Pass `kind` to ask for one explicitly. Runs spend your own agent quota, not Shipeasy credits.

**Use case:** A trail is created from a feature request; start an agent on it to plan it, approve the plan, then start it again to build.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | Which coding agent to fire — `claude`, `cursor`, `copilot` or `jules`. Omitted, the project's coding-agent trigger. |
| `connectorId` | optional | `string` | A specific trigger connector to fire. Overrides `agent`. |
| `kind` | optional | `"plan" \| "build" \| "replan"` | Which run to fire. Omitted, the server picks — `plan` while the trail has no approved plan, else `build`. Asking for `build` before the plan is approved is refused with `409`, and so is asking for `plan` once one is approved: edit the plan, or fire `replan`. `replan` is allowed only once a plan is approved: a read-only run that re-reads the goal metric, the items' outcomes and project memory and submits the next revision, which waits as `drafted` for approval. |
| `prompt` | optional | `string` | Extra instructions appended to the trail prompt. _(length 0–8000)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `AGENT_NOT_CONNECTED` — The named AI agent type has no connected trigger connector in this project — list the available agents (`ops agents list` / `GET /api/admin/agent-profiles`) and use one of those, or connect the agent under Settings → Triggers.
- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_submit_eval`

**Submit a review agent's eval**

Record one review agent's result on one push of a change: a `value` (0–100 for a score agent, 1/0 for a boolean one), a short `rationale`, and any `findings`. The verdict (pass / warn / fail) is computed from the agent's threshold and polarity. Submitting again for the same push replaces the earlier result and the open findings it raised. `prUrl` selects the change; omitted, the trail's primary change.

A review run may also report the product `resources` the diff uses (`getFlag("x")`, `getExperiment("y")`, `t("key")`). They are linked to the trail as detected, and a key that does not exist yet becomes a finding.

The `agentKey` normally names a configured review agent; an unconfigured key is recorded too, as a non-blocking score.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** A review run fired on a push scores the diff for risk and submits `{ agentKey: "risk", value: 35, rationale: "...", findings: [...] }`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `agentKey` | required | `string` | The review agent's key (from `ops review-agents list`). _(length 1–48)_ |
| `value` | required | `number` | 0–100 for a score agent; 1 (yes) or 0 (no) for a boolean one. _(0–100)_ |
| `rationale` | required | `string` | One or two sentences on the evidence behind the value. _(length 1–4000)_ |
| `findings` | optional | `object[]` | Issues to fix, each with a severity, and a file and line when there is one. |
| `prUrl` | optional | `string` | The change reviewed. Omitted, the trail's primary change. _(length 0–500)_ |
| `headSha` | optional | `string` | The commit reviewed. Omitted, the change's latest push. A sha that is not the latest push is recorded against that push, as history. _(length 7–64)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | Your agent type, when you are the review agent. |
| `sessionId` | optional | `string` | Your session id, so the eval can deep-link to the review run. _(length 0–300)_ |
| `resources` | optional | `object[]` | Product resources the reviewed diff uses (`getFlag("x")`, `getExperiment("y")`, `t("key")`). They are linked to the trail as detected. A key that does not exist yet becomes a finding. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_submit_plan`

**Submit a trail's plan**

A plan run submits what it worked out: the plan in markdown, the `release` block (how the trail ships, why, and the exact flags, kill switches, experiments and tracking — events, metrics, alert rules — the build will create; no release tool for `straight_to_main`), the `breakdown` (the milestones and the items, each with its work kind and assignee) and the `sources` it rests on (what it read in project memory and earlier tickets, and what each settled). Submit it once the person has answered any question you asked with `ops questions ask`; the release and its rollout are your choice, with the reason, and the person changes them when they approve. The plan is recorded as `drafted` and waits for a person to approve it; nothing in the breakdown is filed until then. Submitting again replaces a drafted plan; an approved plan is refused with `409` (a person edits it to reopen it), except from a `replan` run, whose submission drafts the next revision with a `summary` of what changed. The open plan or replan run on the trail is closed.

The plan is checked against the trail's release facts (`trails release-facts`). A plan that is incomplete answers `422` with what is missing: an event, metric or alert rule that does not exist and no `tracking` item `creates`, tracking that lands after the work it measures, a `gate` with no `flags` entry (bucketing unit, team stage, cleanup item), an experiment with no metric it `measures`, risks not listed once the plan ships behind a release tool, or a `high` risk with no guard in `detect` or a `rollback` the plan cannot do. A plan that is complete but argued against by the numbers — an experiment the traffic cannot power in 28 days, a first step too thin to prove anything, an operational risk with no kill switch — is accepted, with the warnings kept in `checks` for the person who approves it. On an autopilot trail any warning pauses autopilot and hands the plan to its owner.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** The person picked "behind a flag"; the plan run submits the plan listing the flag `checkout.v2`, bucketed by user with a team stage first, and the risk its error-rate alert guards.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `plan` | required | `string` | The plan in markdown — the approach, the files and repos it touches, the order of the work, how each acceptance criterion is met, and the risks. _(length 1–20000)_ |
| `release` | required | `object` | How the trail ships. The person answers this while the plan is made; the build run creates exactly the resources listed (none for `straight_to_main`), and the Plan gate checks they exist. |
| `release.strategy` | required | `"straight_to_main" \| "flag" \| "flag_experiment" \| "kill_switch" \| "flag_kill_switch" \| "other"` | How the trail ships, as the person chose it while the plan was made — `straight_to_main` (no flag), `flag`, `flag_experiment` (a flag measured by an experiment), `kill_switch` (a kill switch only), `flag_kill_switch`, or `other` (a free-text answer that fits none of those). |
| `release.reason` | required | `string` | One line on why this approach — risk, blast radius, reversibility. _(length 0–2000)_ |
| `release.resources` | required | `object[]` | The flags, kill switches, experiments and tracking (events, metrics, alert rules) to create. No release tool for `straight_to_main`; the strategy fixes which release kinds must be present (a flag for `flag`, a flag and an experiment for `flag_experiment`, and so on). A trail may ship behind several flags; each `ships_behind` flag gets its own rollout, its resource's `rollout` or else this block's. |
| `release.rollout` | optional | `object` | How the flag a trail ships behind is ramped after merge — the release controller's plan (see the design doc, the release controller). Part of the plan's release block; the project's defaults live in `trail-gates` `rollout`. The controller runs on the alerts cron, so a hold shorter than the cron interval rounds up to the next tick. |
| `release.rollout.steps` | required | `number[]` | Percent steps, each above the one before, the last 100. |
| `release.rollout.holdMinutes` | required | `integer` | Minutes a step must stay healthy before the next one. _(0–10080)_ |
| `release.rollout.minExposure` | required | `integer` | Evaluations a step must have served before it counts as healthy, so a quiet hour never passes as a green one. `0` = no floor. _(≥ 0)_ |
| `release.rollout.internal` | optional | `any` | The team stage before any public percent — the project's members are allowlisted on the flag (by email) and the step holds like any other. `null` or absent = no team stage. |
| `release.rollout.guards` | required | `object` | What is watched while a step holds. The trail's `guards` alert-rule resources are watched too. |
| `release.rollout.guards.alertRuleIds` | required | `string[]` | Alert rules (ids) whose firing during a step is a breach. |
| `release.rollout.guards.experimentGuardrails` | required | `boolean` | Whether a breached guardrail of the trail's measuring experiment is a breach. |
| `release.rollout.guards.attributedErrors` | required | `boolean` | Whether a new error attributed to the trail at high confidence is a breach. |
| `release.rollout.policies` | required | `object` | The three rollout decisions — the project defaults unless the creation dialog or a plan edit sets them. |
| `release.rollout.policies.onBreach` | required | `"pull_back" \| "ask_first" \| "ask_then_pull_back"` | What to do when a guard trips during a step — `pull_back` (pull the flag back, investigate and suggest a fix, tell the owner; the default), `ask_first` (ask the owner, only notify), or `ask_then_pull_back` (ask, and pull back after `breachTimeoutMinutes` with no answer). |
| `release.rollout.policies.breachTimeoutMinutes` | required | `integer` | With `ask_then_pull_back`, minutes the owner has before the controller pulls back. _(1–1440)_ |
| `release.rollout.policies.advance` | required | `"auto" \| "ask"` | Whether a healthy step advances by itself (`auto`) or waits for the owner to say so (`ask`). |
| `release.rollout.policies.afterFix` | required | `"resume" \| "ask" \| "restart"` | What happens when the fix merges — `resume` from the last healthy step, `ask` the owner first, or `restart` from the first step. |
| `release.flags` | optional | `object[]` | How each `gate` in `resources` is rolled out beyond its ramp — what it buckets on, the team stage, the item that removes it. One entry per gate. |
| `release.risks` | optional | `object[]` | What could go wrong, how it would be seen and how it is undone. Required once the plan ships behind a release tool or has more than two items. |
| `breakdown` | optional | `object` | The milestones and items a plan breaks the trail into. Nothing is filed while the plan is a draft; approving creates the milestones and files the items. `workKind` defaults to `code`. |
| `breakdown.milestones` | required | `object[]` | The milestones, in order. |
| `breakdown.items` | required | `object[]` | The items, each in at most one milestone. |
| `marketing` | optional | `object` | The plan's marketing strategy — tracked, never executed. Every channel is also a breakdown item of the same title with `workKind` `marketing`, so it has an owner, a status and a place on the timeline. |
| `marketing.summary` | required | `string` | Positioning and audience in a paragraph — who it is for and what it says. _(length 0–2000)_ |
| `marketing.channels` | required | `object[]` | — |
| `sources` | optional | `object[]` | What the plan rests on in project memory (`ops memory search`) and earlier tickets and trails, each with what it settled. |
| `summary` | optional | `string` | For a replan, what changed since the last approved revision. Recorded on the revision. _(length 0–500)_ |
| `goal` | optional | `any` | The metric the plan says will judge the trail, with its baseline and target — sent when the intent is an outcome and the trail has no goal yet. It becomes the trail's goal only while the trail has none (a goal a person set is never replaced), and its metric must already exist; leave `metric` out when a tracking item creates it. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `INVALID_TRANSITION` — The requested lifecycle transition is not allowed from the current state.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_timeline`

**Read a trail's timeline**

Everything that happened on the trail, newest first: created, plans approved, questions asked and answered (on the trail and on its items), runs, items filed and done, pull requests opened, approved and merged, every rollout step, pull-back and autopilot action, the goal watched and met or missed, errors attributed. Each event says whether it was a **decision** — a choice a person (or autopilot on a person's authority) made — and a decided question carries every option it offered and which one was picked.

Pass `decisions=true` for the decisions only. Page with `before` (the `next` of the previous page).

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** Before re-planning, an agent reads what was tried and decided on the trail so the next revision does not repeat it.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `before` | optional | `string` | ISO-8601 time; only events strictly before it (the `next` of the previous page). _(length 1–40)_ |
| `limit` | optional | `integer` | Most events to return (1-200). Defaults to 50. _(1–200)_ |
| `decisions` | optional | `boolean` | Only the decisions. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.

### `trails_unlink_pr`

**Unlink a pull request from a trail**

Detach a pull request from the trail. Its recorded pushes, evals, findings and approvals stay in history but no longer count toward the trail's gates. A merged change cannot be unlinked.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `prUrl` | required | `string` | The pull request's URL. _(length 1–500)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).

### `trails_update`

**Change a trail**

Change a trail's title, intent, type, priority, owner (the lead), repo scope, start and target dates, health, goal or autopilot. Pass at least one field; the rest are left as they are. Changing the type changes which release gates apply.

**Health.** `health` sets it by hand and it holds until changed; `health: null` goes back to the derived value (off track past the target date or while a rollout is fixing, at risk near the target with progress under 75 % or with a high finding or item open, otherwise on track).

**Autopilot.** `autopilot: { enabled, limits }` turns autopilot on or off and sets its limits. Turning it on needs the `autopilot` capability and a person's identity, and makes the caller the accountable approver (`403` otherwise). Turning it off is open to the trail's owner, the person who authorized it and admins.

**Use case:** The acceptance criteria changed after a review — update the body so the next agent run builds the right thing.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `title` | optional | `string` | — _(length 1–200; pattern `^\S(.*\S)?$`)_ |
| `body` | optional | `string` | — _(length 0–20000)_ |
| `type` | optional | `"feature" \| "bug" \| "task"` | What a trail is shipping. A `feature` trail is held to the rollback and measured release gates. |
| `priority` | optional | `any` | Triage priority; `null` clears it. |
| `ownerId` | optional | `any` | The `users.id` of the person owner; `null` unassigns. |
| `ownerConnectorId` | optional | `any` | The agent connector owner; `null` unassigns. |
| `repos` | optional | `string[]` | Replaces the trail's repo scope. |
| `startDate` | optional | `any` | The calendar day work starts (`YYYY-MM-DD`); `null` clears it. |
| `targetDate` | optional | `any` | The calendar day the trail is meant to ship by (`YYYY-MM-DD`); `null` clears it. |
| `health` | optional | `any` | Set the health by hand; `null` goes back to the derived health. |
| `goal` | optional | `any` | Replaces the trail's goal; `null` clears it. |
| `autopilot` | optional | `object` | Turn a trail's autopilot on or off, and set the limits it acts inside. Turning it ON needs the `autopilot` capability (admins have it) and a person's identity — a dashboard session or a signed-in CLI, never an ops key, an admin key or MCP — and makes that person the accountable approver. Turning it off is open to the trail's owner, whoever authorized it, and admins. |
| `autopilot.enabled` | required | `boolean` | Whether autopilot is on. |
| `autopilot.limits` | optional | `object` | Limits to set; each one omitted keeps the trail's current value (the project's default for a new trail). |
| `autopilot.limits.maxRisk` | optional | `any` | — |
| `autopilot.limits.repos` | optional | `string[]` | — |
| `autopilot.limits.types` | optional | `"feature" \| "bug" \| "task"[]` | — |
| `autopilot.limits.maxFixRounds` | optional | `integer` | — _(0–10)_ |
| `autopilot.limits.maxPullBacks` | optional | `integer` | — _(0–10)_ |
| `autopilot.limits.maxRuns` | optional | `integer` | — _(0–100)_ |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.

### `trails_update_finding`

**Resolve or dismiss a finding**

Set a finding's status — `resolved` (it was fixed; say how in `reason`), `dismissed` (it is not a problem; say why), or back to `open`. A finding that is real but out of scope is not dismissed: promote it with `trails promote-finding`.

Safe for the restricted ops key.

**Use case:** The coding agent fixed a flagged issue, pushed, and resolves the finding with `reason: "fixed in abc1234"`.

_Parameters_

| Parameter | | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `handle` | required | `string` | The trail's handle (`T-12`) or its id. _(length 1–64; pattern `^(?:T-[0-9]+\|[0-9a-fA-F-]{32,36})$`)_ |
| `findingId` | required | `string` | A resource path identifier — an opaque `xxx_<ULID>` id (~30 chars) or the resource's `name`/`key`. 1–128 characters; the upper bound matches the longest name/key any resource accepts, so an over-long value can never name a real row. _(length 1–128)_ |
| `status` | required | `"open" \| "resolved" \| "dismissed"` | A finding stays `open` until it is `resolved` (fixed) or `dismissed` (not a problem). A finding raised on an earlier push is reported `stale` but stays open until somebody decides. |
| `reason` | optional | `string` | Why — the fixing commit, or why it is not a problem. _(length 0–2000)_ |
| `agent` | optional | `"jarvis" \| "claude" \| "cursor" \| "copilot" \| "jules"` | Your agent type, when an agent is resolving the finding. |

_Errors_ — beyond the [common errors](#errors):

- `BAD_REQUEST` — Malformed request (bad JSON, missing project scope).
- `NOT_FOUND` — The resource does not exist or is not visible to the caller.
- `VALIDATION` — The request body failed structural (schema) validation.
